guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by kiting Undertow axes with E slows, shielding his burst, and all-inning only when he is already low; Olaf wins any extended trade and runs her down during Ragnarok at any score.

keyTips.text: Kite axes or die. Dodge Undertow and never stand near the landed axe, because picking it up refunds his chase and he can run you down from full health.
keyTips.heading: Axe kite

keyTips.text: Shield burst, then leave instantly. W into him to block Undertow plus Reckless Swing damage, Q straight back out, and let your E slow keep him off you.
keyTips.heading: Block and leave

keyTips.text: Never take extended trades. His sustain, attack speed at low health, and raw stats win every long fight, so repeat short combos until he is low enough to finish.
keyTips.heading: No long fights

tips.text: Before level 6, kite with E slows and Q pokes. Keep cooldowns up before stepping forward, because one axe hit without dashes ready is a death.
tips.heading: Pre-6 kite

tips.text: Respect his low-health turn. Vicious Strikes shield and healing flip all-ins you thought were lethal, so confirm the kill before committing everything.
tips.heading: Low-health turn

tips.text: If you fall behind, play safe without tilting. He snowballs through mistakes, but you outscale him; quiet farming minutes close his window.
tips.heading: Safe scaling

tips.text: During Ragnarok ({cd:2:R}), only kite. He is immune to your slows and suppression peel while it lasts, so spend dashes surviving and fight when it fades.
tips.heading: Ragnarok kite

tips.text: Read his build before dueling. Ravenous Hydra sustain demands anti-heal thinking, Stridebreaker slows demand dash discipline, and Blade of the Ruined King demands shorter trades.
tips.heading: Build read

tips.text: Win by never letting him touch you. Axe dodges and E slows starve his whole kit, and your scaling teamfight picks outvalue his run-at-you fights.
tips.heading: Touch denial

tips.text: Punish mistakes even when he is behind. Like other run-down bruisers he kills careless targets at any score, so keep the kite perfect until fights group.
tips.heading: Mistake punish

itemization.text: Build Eclipse first on the Phase Rush line. Phase Rush plus E slows is your kite engine, and Eclipse shields the one axe combo that reaches you.
Start Doran's Blade with Teleport and Flash. Blade funds early pokes, Flash is mandatory to escape axe chases, and Teleport recovers the lane after his ultimate.
Take Phase Rush with Inspiration secondary runes. The speed burst after your short combo is what keeps his axes and Ragnarok from ever connecting.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by baiting Disdain and abusing its cooldown, kiting his shotgun knees, and shielding Corrosive Charge; Urgot wins any trade his flip starts and executes careless targets from high health.

keyTips.text: Bait or dodge Disdain, then trade freely. His E flip is his only engage; sidestep it and his spent cooldown is your window for full combos.
keyTips.heading: Flip bait

keyTips.text: Do not burst through his flip shield early. When Disdain gives him a shield, wait it out instead of feeding damage into it, then punish the cooldown.
keyTips.heading: Shield wait

keyTips.text: Kite around his shotgun knees. Circle him so the same leg cannons stay spent, because walking straight lines lets every Echoing Flames passive blast you.
keyTips.heading: Knee kite

tips.text: Against good Urgots, never greed an auto in your combo. E in and instantly Q away, because the extra auto is the moment his flip catches you.
tips.heading: No greed

tips.text: Shield Corrosive Charge on reaction. W blocks his Q poke and the slow mark his Purge wants, keeping his shotgun chase from starting.
tips.heading: Charge shield

tips.text: If you misplay, R through his flip. Your unstoppable blink bypasses the Disdain stun, turning his one engage into your escape or counter-kill.
tips.heading: Blink save

tips.text: Respect his execute math forever. Fear Beyond Death ({cd:6:R}) plus Ignite kills from around seventy percent against careless targets, so track both before trading low.
tips.heading: Execute math

tips.text: Beware the flip-Flash surprise. Good Urgots extend Disdain with Flash into ultimate; keep your own Flash or R ready when his sum is up.
tips.heading: Flip flash

tips.text: Win the flip economy. Every dodged Disdain is a free combo, and without flips he cannot hold you in Purge or shotgun range.
tips.heading: Flip economy

tips.text: Outscale into team picks. Suppress carries with R while he walks at fights, and force him to execute frontliners instead of your team.
tips.heading: Team picks

itemization.text: Rush Serpent's Fang when his flip shield and team shields matter. Cutting Disdain's shield restores your trade math in every punish window.
Start Doran's Shield with Flash and Teleport. Shield survives Corrosive Charge poke, and Teleport recovers you after the one flip combo that lands.
Build Eclipse after your shield answer. It sustains the longer Purge trades while your flip-bait combos keep winning the lane.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by trading after his empowered Transfusion, shielding Tides of Blood, and bursting after Sanguine Pool; Vladimir wins by outsustaining sloppy lanes and outscaling bruiser builds late.

keyTips.text: Trade after his empowered Transfusion, never into it. His crimson Q chunks and heals him; once it fades his early damage and healing are both weak, so strike then.
keyTips.heading: Crimson window

keyTips.text: Shield Tides of Blood on reaction. W blocks his charged E burst, and your E-empowered-auto-Q combo abuses his short range whenever he steps up.
keyTips.heading: Tide shield

keyTips.text: Burst after Sanguine Pool, before his ultimate pops. Pool spent means no escape; kill him inside Hemoplague's fuse instead of letting it heal him back.
keyTips.heading: Pool punish

tips.text: Make the lane volatile on purpose. His early sustain is weak, so repeated short combos deny the free scaling farm he wants, but respect his Q-Ignite burst trades.
tips.heading: Volatile lane

tips.text: Learn how he pools in the first trades. If he panics Pool early, bait it and all-in on cooldown; if he holds it, save burst and farm your spike.
tips.heading: Pool read

tips.text: Abuse his short range. He must walk close to farm and poke, so E in with an empowered auto and Q out whenever he oversteps your casters.
tips.heading: Range abuse

tips.text: He outscales bruiser builds, so lethality evens the game. Burst him or his carries before his teamfight healing takes over long fights.
tips.heading: Lethality scale

tips.text: One mistake feeds his snowball. A death here lets him bully the rest of lane, so keep trades disciplined even while playing aggressively.
tips.heading: No donations

tips.text: Win by ending his scaling clock early. Kills and priority before his items make his late-game healing arrive too late to save his team.
tips.heading: Clock win

tips.text: In fights, burst him after Pool or ignore him for carries. R a carry while he waits out his rotation, and never let Hemoplague heal through a long fight.
tips.heading: Fight burst

itemization.text: Rush Voltaic Cyclosword on the lethality line. Burst plus slow sticks you to a short-range mage whose escape is one Pool per fight.
Add Hexdrinker or Maw of Malmortius if his burst starts winning. The magic shield survives his full rotation while your trades keep pressuring.
Start Doran's Blade with Flash and Ignite. Blade funds early volatile trades, and Ignite cuts the healing his whole lane depends on.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by punishing a drain that does not include her and interrupting Bountiful Harvest with R; Fiddlesticks wins through sustain, low-health execute damage, and unseen Crowstorm engages.

keyTips.text: When he starts Bountiful Harvest on minions without tethering you, take a short Electrocute trade. Do not walk into a fresh drain simply because he is standing still near the wave.
keyTips.heading: Wave-only drain

keyTips.text: R him during Bountiful Harvest to interrupt the channel. This denies the completed-channel cooldown refund, leaving a longer punish window based on {cd:9:W}.
keyTips.heading: Interrupt the refund

keyTips.text: Use R predictively when Terrify is about to hit so the fear arrives during your unstoppable cast. This is a timing answer, not a way to cast R after you are already feared.
keyTips.heading: Fear timing

tips.text: Respect his early drain instead of forcing constant contact. Later, your ability to interrupt W helps the duel, but vision still decides whether Crowstorm overturns a teamfight.
tips.heading: Drain and vision

tips.text: Do not continue a low-health trade into the end of Bountiful Harvest. Its final hit deals missing-health damage, so what looks like a small remaining drain can still finish you.
tips.heading: Low-health drain danger

tips.text: When short trades have lowered him, apply Ignite before committing the all-in. Leave room for his fear to push you away rather than relying on one uninterrupted melee chase through his healing.
tips.heading: Ignite finish

tips.text: From level 6, keep vision on the brushes and approaches beside the wave before pushing. Crowstorm ({cd:9:R}) makes an unseen flank far more dangerous than another ordinary lane poke.
tips.heading: Level-6 fog check

tips.text: Ping when he leaves lane and warn the direction of his possible gank. A neutral lane is not a win if he turns the next unseen Crowstorm into kills on your teammates.
tips.heading: Missing-lane warning

tips.text: When he is pushing without a protected retreat, bring your jungler into the lane rather than forcing another solo drain trade. Coordinate the catch so fear and healing do not simply reset the attempt.
tips.heading: Gank the exposed lane

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and build Voltaic Cyclosword with Electrocute. Your damage is for the short window around a wave-only drain or interrupted W, not for standing in Bountiful Harvest.
itemization.heading: Burst route

itemization.text: Build Maw of Malmortius if his magic damage is preventing you from safely farming or contesting. It helps reach the later-game matchup without gambling on another low-health drain fight.
itemization.heading: Magic safety

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by bullying her before level 6, baiting Divine Judgment and re-engaging, and holding wave priority for skirmishes; Kayle wins only by free-farming to her late-game ascension.

keyTips.text: Bully her before level 6 without spending every dash. E in, empowered auto, Q out on repeat, but keep one dash back because Lethal Tempo plus her passive can run you down.
keyTips.heading: Bully combo

keyTips.text: Bait Divine Judgment, then re-engage with R. Burst her until she ults herself, leave, and R back in the moment her invulnerability ends.
keyTips.heading: Ult bait

keyTips.text: Reaction-test her ultimate. R her suddenly and fire Q immediately; if she fails to ult in time, your burst plus Electrocute lands before she can answer, and if she does ult, dash out and come back the moment it ends.
keyTips.heading: Reaction test

tips.text: Deny farm, do not donate kills. She should leave lane behind on gold even when she plays perfectly, so zone her from the wave without dashing under her turret.
tips.heading: Farm denial

tips.text: After level 6, trade after she spends Q or W. Radiant Blast slow and Celestial Blessing speed are her escape tools, so combo only when one is freshly spent.
tips.heading: Cooldown trades

tips.text: Respect her Starfire Spellblade execute. It hits harder the lower you are, so top off with potions before trading instead of sitting at half health.
tips.heading: Execute respect

tips.text: Hold priority and move first. Push her in and win skirmishes with your team while she is stuck farming for her ascension under turret.
tips.heading: First move

tips.text: Stop her turret scaling. Shove waves with a teammate before objectives so she cannot free-farm side lanes while you group, and punish her when she steps up alone.
tips.heading: Turret denial

tips.text: Win before her late game arrives. Your mid-game R picks and skirmish power must close the game while she still needs items and levels to carry.
tips.heading: Close early

tips.text: In fights, delete her before Divine Judgment saves the dive. Burst her first or bait the ultimate early, because a saved Kayle ult turns your pick into her teamfight.
tips.heading: Ult first

itemization.text: Rush Voltaic Cyclosword on the lethality line. Its slow keeps you on a champion whose escape is movement speed, and burst ends her before Lethal Tempo stacks.
Start Doran's Blade, or Long Sword with Refillable Potion to rush your spike. Blade funds the early bully trades; the long-sword start reaches Voltaic sooner when you farm cleanly.
Take Flash and Ignite. Ignite pressures the early levels she must survive, and Flash covers the one Lethal Tempo chase you misjudge.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by preserving health through the opening levels, keeping retreat spells, and coordinating crowd control; Master Yi wins extended chases, defensive Meditate baits, and takedown resets.

keyTips.text: Kite backward through level 1 and avoid a heavy opening trade. Losing most of your health immediately gives Yi a level-2 dive opportunity before your defensive kit is available.
keyTips.heading: Healthy first level

keyTips.text: Track his Double Strike attacks before walking up for Q poke. If the extra attack is ready, expect him to use that moment to begin the trade rather than treating it as an ordinary auto.
keyTips.heading: Double Strike check

keyTips.text: R can interrupt Meditate, but do not throw it while Alpha Strike can make Yi untargetable. Bait his Q first when possible so your main crowd control does not disappear into his dodge.
keyTips.heading: Ultimate versus Q

tips.text: Treat this as an off-meta top-lane duel with real early kill pressure. Preserve enough health to reach level 3, then use short shielded trades instead of racing his autos through an extended fight.
tips.heading: Survive the opening

tips.text: From level 3, W his damage and use your dashes to leave after a brief exchange. Wait for the full basic kit rather than forcing the same trade while you still lack a defensive spell.
tips.heading: Third-level defense

tips.text: Use light Q poke without spending both W and E to travel forward. Keep those tools for getting back out so a forward trade cannot become a long chase and another dive setup.
tips.heading: Keep the retreat spells

tips.text: Hold the main burst while Yi channels Meditate ({cd:11:W}). He can use its damage reduction to erase your rotation; punish an early W spent as an attack reset instead.
tips.heading: Meditate restraint

tips.text: Respect Highlander from level 6 and avoid a long all-in with your spells spent. His movement and attack speed let him run you down; prioritize dash distance instead of expecting E's slow to stop him.
tips.heading: Level-6 chase

tips.text: Favor coordinated teamfights over the later side-lane duel. Use your team's crowd control to focus Yi before a takedown grants him the resets that let him keep chasing.
tips.heading: Stop the resets

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and build Voltaic Cyclosword with Electrocute. The damage is for a clean opening after his defenses are spent, not for racing Highlander attacks.
itemization.heading: Short-trade burst

itemization.text: Take Shield Bash and Bone Plating with Flash and Teleport. Bone Plating helps the opening contact, while Flash gives an exit when an aggressive dash would otherwise let Yi stay in attack range.
itemization.heading: Safe lane setup

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by sidestepping every Decimating Smash and melting his health bar with sweet-spot Q hits; Sion wins only by landing charged smashes from fog of war or dragging fights into his death passive.

keyTips.text: Sidestep Decimating Smash every time. Dash sideways as the axe rises instead of backing in a straight line, and punish the spent smash with a full combo.
keyTips.heading: Smash sidestep

keyTips.text: Land sweet-spot Q hits as your main damage. Against his health stacking, the outer-edge Q damage is the tool that actually melts him, so space every cast for the edge.
keyTips.heading: Sweet spots

keyTips.text: Save a dash for his death. When you kill him, Glory in Death keeps him hitting, so keep one dash to leave his passive range instead of trading with the corpse.
keyTips.heading: Death dash

tips.text: Watch bushes and fog constantly. Sion players charge Decimating Smash from brush where you cannot see the cast, so ward lane brush and never face-check it on his timing.
tips.heading: Brush watch

tips.text: Expect early smash releases from good Sions. If he drops the axe early to clip you, shorten your trades and keep dashing sideways rather than holding for the full charge.
tips.heading: Early release

tips.text: If he slows you with Roar of the Slayer right before dying, wait out the slow before finishing him. Killing him while slowed leaves you in reach of his death passive autos.
tips.heading: Slow wait

tips.text: Once he stacks enough health, stop forcing the duel. A Sion too tanky to kill still loses fights when you ignore him and R his backline, so take plates and rotate.
tips.heading: Ignore and rotate

tips.text: In fights it can be your job to kill him. Sweet-spot Q damage melts health stackers faster than most of your team, so peel him off your carries with repeated edge hits.
tips.heading: Tank duty

tips.text: Win by never eating a charged smash. Without Decimating Smash knockups he cannot start a trade, and your dash uptime keeps every later fight on your angle.
tips.heading: Smash denial

tips.text: Convert health leads into his team. Suppress a carry with R while he lumbers toward the fight, and finish teamfights before his passive and second health bar matter.
tips.heading: Carry picks

itemization.text: Rush Serpent's Fang when he leans on Soul Furnace shields. Cutting the shield in every trade keeps your sweet-spot damage sticking instead of bouncing off his W.
Build Eclipse into Black Cleaver against health stacking. Cleaver shred stacks fast through your multi-hit combos, and Eclipse keeps your trades winning as his health grows.
Start Doran's Shield or Blade with Teleport and Flash. Shield plus Second Wind survives his poke if you struggle with smash timings; Blade funds early kills when you dodge cleanly.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins through one-sided Q poke, denying repeat contact, and fighting with her team; Warwick wins through sustained healing, defensive bait, and side-lane chases.

keyTips.text: Only attempt the all-in when Primal Howl ({cd:19:E}) and Barrier are down and your burst can finish him. A half-health Warwick with either defense ready can reverse an apparently winning fight.
keyTips.heading: Defensive gate

keyTips.text: When Warwick launches Infinite Duress from far away, react with R to deny the suppression during your unstoppable cast. Keep watching his approach rather than casting after he has already pinned you.
keyTips.heading: Answer the leap

keyTips.text: If he reaches you, W his damage and E away immediately. Do not remain beside him for extra autos; your shield and slow are there to end his access to you.
keyTips.heading: Contact escape

tips.text: Warwick sitting near half health is normal, not proof that he is ready to die. Treat Primal Howl and Barrier as part of his remaining health before committing your burst.
tips.heading: Health is deceptive

tips.text: Use Q at its outer reach and leave before Warwick can turn the exchange into repeated attacks. Keep the lane trade to damage he cannot freely heal back by hitting you.
tips.heading: One-sided poke

tips.text: Time W for Jaws of the Beast rather than only for his first auto. Good Warwick players can follow your movement with held Q, so a dash alone is not a dependable answer to his bite.
tips.heading: Predict the bite

tips.text: Once he has Blade of the Ruined King, favor teamfights over side-lane duels. An even Warwick can still win the sustained 1v1 despite being less effective when your team can focus him.
tips.heading: Blade side lane

tips.text: After you collect safely and deny his lane kills, watch his route out of top. Ping his roams and jungle invades so your safe lane does not become a lead for him elsewhere.
tips.heading: Warn the invade

tips.text: Preserve farm and use Flash defensively rather than gambling on an early solo kill. An unfed Warwick is easier to handle in grouped fights, where your team can stop him before he keeps attacking and healing.
tips.heading: Deny the snowball

itemization.text: Buy Executioner's Calling early. Its physical-damage Grievous Wounds matters against his Q and passive healing even when you also brought Ignite.
itemization.heading: Early healing cut

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade into Eclipse with Conqueror, Shield Bash, and Bone Plating. Keep Teleport and Flash for the safe lane; Eclipse's shield helps a short trade but does not let you outlast his repeated attacks.
itemization.heading: Safer bruiser setup

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by kiting Spinning Slash with W and E, zoning him off Fury, and controlling waves; Tryndamere wins any dive after one early kill and stat-checks side lanes forever.

keyTips.text: Kite backwards with abilities, never auto-trade. When he spins onto you, W and E away at once; standing to fight his Fury autos loses at every stage.
keyTips.heading: Backwards kite

keyTips.text: Read his keystone before trading. Grasp means short poke autos to outsustain you, Hail of Blades means a spin plus three fast autos to react to, and Lethal Tempo means never extend.
keyTips.heading: Rune read

keyTips.text: Zone him when his Fury is empty. Without Fury he loses crit chance and sustain, so step up and deny minions in that window instead of respecting him.
keyTips.heading: Fury zoning

tips.text: Wave control decides this lane. Freeze on him and you dictate trades; let waves push to you badly and he dives with Undying Rage and snowballs.
If he freezes on you, consider proxying. Breaking his freeze behind his turret beats walking into his spin range and donating a dive setup.
tips.heading: Freeze break

tips.text: Respect Ghost and Ignite run-downs. His chase kills from full health when your dashes are spent, so never trade deep without an exit.
tips.heading: Chase respect

tips.text: After his first item, expect heavy trades into dives. He heals back with sustain, then dives with ultimate, so keep your health and dashes topped.
tips.heading: Dive watch

tips.text: Push waves before objectives, then Teleport back. He will tax side turrets while you group, so clear first and answer his split with numbers.
tips.heading: Wave first

tips.text: Win by never giving the first death. One kill turns him into a permanent side-lane stat-check; a starved Tryndamere only annoys turrets your team can defend.
tips.heading: Death denial

tips.text: In fights he matters least. Suppress his carries with R while he spins at your frontline, and end fights before he cleans up low targets.
tips.heading: Fight value

itemization.text: Rush Death's Dance, starting with two Cloth Armors. Its armor and bleed-out passive make his all-ins survivable and his trades finally losable for him.
Add Plated Steelcaps against his auto damage. Tabis blunt the Fury crit autos that win his extended trades.
Start Doran's Blade with Flash and Exhaust. Blade funds early Fury zoning, and Exhaust blunts the Ghost all-in his ultimate otherwise guarantees.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by answering Leap Strike and Counter Strike with the correct dash every time and all-inning only while Counter Strike is down; Jax wins the moment one answer is wrong, even when behind.

keyTips.text: Memorize these three answers. If he only leaps with Q, W away. If he starts Counter Strike on top of you, E out. If he leaps with Counter Strike active, answer with W into Q, or W into E when Q is spent.
keyTips.heading: Three answers

keyTips.text: Poke with Q only while both W and E stay ready. Aggression without both answers up is how a winning lane gets stunned and run down.
keyTips.heading: Poke discipline

keyTips.text: Use R to deny the Counter Strike stun. Its unstoppable blink lets you damage him through the sequence instead of eating the stun at the end of it.
keyTips.heading: R unstoppable

tips.text: Kite backward with E whenever he leaps without Counter Strike. A leap answered cleanly leaves him in your wave with no way to stick.
tips.heading: Leap kite

tips.text: Shield his Counter Strike with W when E is unavailable, then leave before the stun pops. Half-answers still lose the trade, so commit to the full exit.
tips.heading: Shield answer

tips.text: Expect the lane to sharpen after level 3 once he holds both Leap Strike and Counter Strike together. Judge every trade from that point by whether both of your answers are ready, not by how the first two levels went.
tips.heading: Post-3 trades

tips.text: All-in only while Counter Strike ({cd:24:E}) is down. That single cooldown is his entire defense against your burst sequence.
tips.heading: All-in window

tips.text: Keep answering his engage the same way even when ahead: W away from a leap alone, E out when Counter Strike starts on top of you, and W into Q when he leaps with Counter Strike active. One stunned combo from behind lets him stack Relentless Assault and stat-check the rest of the fight.
tips.heading: No autopilot

tips.text: Win by never giving him a stunned target. Without the stun he cannot stack attack speed on you, and your poke plus short trades grind him out of lane.
tips.heading: Stun denial

tips.text: Convert Counter Strike downtime into plates, wave crashes or R picks. His leap alone cannot answer your ultimate engage once his dodge is spent.
tips.heading: Downtime plays

itemization.text: Build Eclipse first on the bruiser line even while running Electrocute. The rune wins the lane trades, but you need bruiser durability to survive the one Jax combo you eventually misanswer.
Start Doran's Blade with Flash and Ignite. Early kill pressure before his scaling stacks matter is how this lane stays playable.
Take Bone Plating and Shield Bash as your Resolve secondary runes. Bone Plating blunts his leap burst, and Shield Bash pays you back every time W answers his engage.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by keeping her waves, shielding Fling, and coordinating proxy catches; Singed wins when she chases poison long enough to lose farm or walks into a grounded fling.

keyTips.text: Walk to lane with your level-1 minions and make his first proxy attempt awkward. If he gets past you, collecting the wave under turret is better than abandoning it for an uncertain chase.
keyTips.heading: Escort the first wave

keyTips.text: W before Fling lands to absorb its damage, then use E to catch and slow him after you land. Check where the throw will put you before deciding that following him is safe.
keyTips.heading: Fling answer

keyTips.text: Dash away from Mega Adhesive's landing area before it grounds you. Do not spend all your movement approaching Singed and leave him an easy W placement on your retreat.
keyTips.heading: Move before the ground

tips.text: Pressure Singed without following him on a long route through Poison Trail. Proxy catches are worthwhile when your wave is covered and your jungler can help, not when they cost you the lane's farm.
tips.heading: Wave before chase

tips.text: If Mega Adhesive catches you, you can still cast your basic damage and shield abilities without taking a passive dash. Keep using Q, W, or E as appropriate instead of treating the grounding field as a silence.
tips.heading: Grounded spell casts

tips.text: Poke with Q and kite back while your other abilities recover. Do not run after Singed through Poison Trail with no spells available to damage him or escape a Fling.
tips.heading: No cooldown chase

tips.text: When Singed proxies, coordinate with your jungler and use R to pin him before he executes. Only take the catch while your incoming wave is covered, so a failed chase does not pay him in lost farm.
tips.heading: Proxy catch

tips.text: Avoid repeatedly conceding the shove when you can safely clear. Priority limits the time Singed has to slip behind your next wave and establish another proxy.
tips.heading: Keep wave priority

tips.text: Ping Singed's exits from lane and look to countergank when your wave is handled. If he keeps proxying instead, counter-proxying can preserve your income without following him through poison.
tips.heading: Answer his roams

itemization.text: Choose Doran's Shield if Poison Trail chip is wearing you down, or Doran's Blade if you can keep short trades favorable. Take Electrocute so a brief Fling response pays off without a long chase.
itemization.heading: Start for the lane

itemization.text: Build Eclipse for a shielded bruiser exchange or Voltaic Cyclosword for burst when a coordinated R catch is realistic. Neither purchase makes chasing a full-health Singed through poison a good use of your wave.
itemization.heading: First-item route

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by dodging every Rupture, taking only short post-dodge trades against AP builds, and holding lane priority; Cho'Gath wins by silencing her in fights and deleting carries with Feast.

keyTips.text: Dodge Rupture or lose the matchup. Predict and dash the knockup circle every time; it is the cast his whole combo and kill threat hangs on.
keyTips.heading: Rupture dodge

keyTips.text: Do not hold W into his silence. Feral Scream silences you before your shield answers, so dash first and W only outside his cone.
keyTips.heading: Silence respect

keyTips.text: Keep trades short after every dodge. Land your combo and leave before Vorpal Spikes autos and his next Rupture cycle turn the trade.
keyTips.heading: Short trades

tips.text: Hold priority and pressure from level 1. You dictate the wave while he waits on Rupture, so crash, poke, and make him farm under turret.
tips.heading: Early pressure

tips.text: Fear AP Cho'Gath specifically. Ability-power builds with Hail of Blades burst through sloppy spacing, so only trade after Rupture is spent and respect his silence range.
tips.heading: AP fear

tips.text: One mistake still kills you. A landed Rupture into silence, spikes, and Feast ({cd:31:R}) deletes even ahead Ambessas, so never trade without a dash.
tips.heading: Mistake price

tips.text: In teamfights, expect his silence on you. Enter after Feral Scream is spent or flank his carries, because a silenced Ambessa gets bursted before dashing.
tips.heading: Silence entry

tips.text: A great Cho'Gath scales into a shutdown tank. If he reaches that point, stop hunting him and R his carries while he lumbers between fights.
tips.heading: Carry pivot

tips.text: Win by making Rupture whiff all game. Without knockups he cannot start fights or protect carries, and your priority controls every objective setup.
tips.heading: Whiff control

tips.text: Close before his stacks peak. Feast stacks make him unkillable late, so convert early priority into turrets and picks on his team.
tips.heading: Stack clock

itemization.text: Build Eclipse first against tank Cho'Gath. Its shield and sustain win the short trades while you wait out his cooldown cycles.
Rush Black Cleaver if he buys armor first. If he greedily stacks health with no armor, Eclipse damage already suffices and Cleaver can wait.
Start Doran's Blade with Teleport and Flash. Blade funds early priority trades, and Teleport recovers you after the one Rupture that eventually lands.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by freezing the returning wave, spacing Q sweet spots, and leaving Heart Zapper before its detonation; Mundo wins if free cleavers and early gold buy him unpunishable sustain.

keyTips.text: Slow-push the opening waves, crash for a short recall, and freeze the returning wave. Make Mundo walk forward to farm instead of letting him collect safely beside his turret.
keyTips.heading: Bounce into a freeze

keyTips.text: Dash out before Heart Zapper detonates. Do not give his W a champion hit that returns more of the damage he stored during your trade.
keyTips.heading: Leave the detonation

keyTips.text: When Mundo walks up for an auto or Blunt Force Trauma, E into him and line up both Q sweet spots. His decision to farm in melee range is your opening to chase.
keyTips.heading: Punish melee farming

tips.text: Build an early wave advantage rather than trading autos into his first health purchases. E into Q sweet spots punishes his farming, while denying plates delays the health and sustain that make him difficult to remove.
tips.heading: Wave and healing control

tips.text: Dodge Infected Bonesaw ({cd:36:Q}) and make him spend it on last hits. On a contested cannon, W can absorb his cleaver while you stand in its path; punish him if he walks closer afterward.
tips.heading: Cleaver economy

tips.text: Watch the low-health minion in front of Mundo. W the corpse he sends through the wave with E rather than letting Blunt Force Trauma poke you down before your next trade.
tips.heading: Minion swat

tips.text: After his first recall with Giant's Belts, stop taking extended trades. Keep using E to set up Q sweet spots rather than trying to win a sustained auto fight into his new health.
tips.heading: Health purchase respect

tips.text: Protect your plates before minute 14 to slow his Warmog's Armor timing. If he later commits to a side lane during a major teamfight, weigh the fight against the tower rather than automatically following him.
tips.heading: Delay his sustain

tips.text: Use R pressure to draw Maximum Dosage ({cd:36:R}), then reassess the dive after his healing ends. Forcing his ultimate is progress; do not treat its activation as permission to finish him immediately.
tips.heading: Force the ultimate first

itemization.text: Choose Eclipse into his Heartsteel health build for shielded trades. Against a health-and-AD build with little armor, Voltaic Cyclosword supports the burst approach; neither choice excuses missed Q sweet spots.
itemization.heading: First item by defenses

itemization.text: Ignite covers early healing when you want lane pressure. After your first completed item, consider Mortal Reminder for physical-damage Grievous Wounds and armor penetration against his growing sustain.
itemization.heading: Healing cut timing

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade when you can dodge cleavers reliably; choose Doran's Shield if Q poke is forcing bad recalls before the first wave bounce.
itemization.heading: Safer start

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins only by dodging Flawless Duet every time, engaging with at most one dash, and punishing her mistakes on bouncing waves; Irelia stat-checks with full passive stacks and wins every extended chase.

keyTips.text: Dodge Flawless Duet or lose. Always hold at least one dash for her stun blades, because the stun into stacked autos is her whole kill threat.
keyTips.heading: Stun dodge

keyTips.text: Never spend more than one dash to engage. She dashes to your wave faster than you reposition, so the second dash you spend forward is the escape you no longer have.
keyTips.heading: One-dash rule

keyTips.text: When she ults, R behind yourself to leave Vanguard's Edge. Escaping the blade wall denies her free Bladesurge resets and the slow that lets her stack on you.
keyTips.heading: Ult escape

tips.text: Expect her to take wave priority. Contest only around large waves of your own, and punish her on waves bouncing back to you where she must overextend to stack her passive.
tips.heading: Wave terms

tips.text: Track what she can dash to. Low-health minions are her roads; stand away from dying casters so her Bladesurge chain cannot reach you for free.
tips.heading: Dash roads

tips.text: Respect her level-up timers. A sudden level edge means full stacks and an all-in, so back off the wave in the seconds before she levels.
tips.heading: Timer respect

tips.text: Respect her Blade of the Ruined King spike. Her first item lets her stat-check even when behind, so shorten trades and keep the Flawless Duet dodge perfect around it.
tips.heading: Blade spike

tips.text: Even ahead, never autopilot. One landed Flawless Duet in the side lane still kills you, so keep playing for grouped picks where your R starts fights she cannot stack in.
tips.heading: No autopilot

tips.text: Win by making Flawless Duet whiff all game. Without the stun she cannot hold you in her passive autos, and your short trades plus R picks decide fights.
tips.heading: Whiff economy

tips.text: After she Bladesurges onto you, strike back with Q2 behind you. Hitting her on the landing side of her dash is the counter-hit that keeps her honest.
tips.heading: Landing punish

itemization.text: Choose Eclipse for bruiser trades or Voltaic Cyclosword for burst. Eclipse survives her stacked autos longer; Voltaic deletes her before stacks matter when you play hit-and-run.
Start Doran's Blade with Flash and Ignite for the aggressive line, killing her in levels 1 to 3 before her stacks rule the lane. Teleport instead is the safe scaling choice.
Take Shield Bash and Bone Plating in Resolve. Bone Plating blunts her first stacked burst, and Shield Bash pays off every W block while you wait out her passive.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by popping his barrels before they chain, punishing Remove Scurvy downtime with R, and trading only while his Trial by Fire passive is down; Gangplank wins barrel chains and passive-empowered run-downs.

keyTips.text: Win the barrel timing duel. Your longer auto reach lets you last-hit Powder Keg barrels before his Parrrley or auto chains them, and a barrel you pop denies his whole trade.
keyTips.heading: Barrel duel

keyTips.text: Punish Remove Scurvy with R. When he oranges out of pressure, his escape is spent, so R onto him before it returns and force the kill or his Flash.
keyTips.heading: Orange punish

keyTips.text: Trade only while Trial by Fire is down. His passive true-damage auto wins any trade it joins, so wait for the burning blade to fade before stepping in.
keyTips.heading: Passive window

tips.text: Respect his level 1 completely. Trial by Fire plus early barrel placement can throw the lane before it starts, so concede the first push and start fighting from level 3.
tips.heading: Level-1 respect

tips.text: Play faster from level 3 onward. Short Electrocute combos punish him between barrels, but leave before a fresh barrel slows you and speeds him up.
tips.heading: Level-3 start

tips.text: If he takes Ignite, respect the run-down. One barrel slow into passive autos plus Ignite kills from health totals that look safe against Teleport Gangplanks.
tips.heading: Ignite respect

tips.text: Match your build to his. Against full-crit Gangplank, lethality burst kills him before barrel chains matter; against bruiser Gangplank, build bruiser and match his longer fights.
tips.heading: Build match

tips.text: Press a lead hard. A squishy Gangplank behind on gold cannot farm safely into your R threat, so crash waves and deny him the safe scaling he wants.
tips.heading: Lead press

tips.text: Starve his scaling by winning barrels and forcing fights on your R. He needs quiet farm to reach his late-game barrel damage, and every orange-forced R trade steals that time.
tips.heading: Time theft

tips.text: In teamfights, R a carry before he chains barrels into your team. His Cannon Barrage ({cd:41:R}) zones grouped fights, so start the fight on your target instead of walking through his zone.
tips.heading: Fight start

itemization.text: Open Eclipse against bruiser Gangplank or Voltaic Cyclosword against crit Gangplank. Eclipse sustains the longer barrel trades; Voltaic burst deletes the squishy build before it chains barrels.
Start Doran's Shield with Flash and Ignite. Shield survives Parrrley poke while you learn his barrel timings, and Ignite gives the early kill pressure his orange otherwise denies.
Take Shield Bash and Second Wind as your Resolve secondary runes. Shield Bash pays off every W block, and Second Wind patches the Parrrley poke between your trades.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins short trades by avoiding Nevermove and shielding Death's Hand; Swain wins if his root or sustained ultimate keeps her fighting after her burst is spent.

keyTips.text: Dodge the returning Nevermove before worrying about Vision of Empire. Avoiding E removes the easy setup that lets him place W on a trapped target.
keyTips.heading: Root into eye

keyTips.text: W his Death's Hand, then use E and Q to trade around him and move back out. Repeat brief exchanges instead of offering your health to his repeated close-range Q casts.
keyTips.heading: Shield the close burst

keyTips.text: After level 6, keep mobility available unless he is low enough for a real kill attempt. Do not spend your last dash entering range and leave yourself stuck beside Demonic Ascension.
keyTips.heading: Save an exit at six

tips.text: Swain's lane is manageable while you can leave after your spells. His level-6 drain and a Frozen Heart rush change the commitment threshold, so do not turn every favorable poke into an all-in.
tips.heading: Short trades before drain

tips.text: Use R before Nevermove or Vision of Empire lands when you need to cover the incoming control with your unstoppable cast. Choose whether the landing gives you an engage or an exit before committing it.
tips.heading: Ultimate through control

tips.text: If you brought Ignite, apply it for the low-health level-6 kill attempt before his drain recovers the damage. Enter with your full burst available instead of spending healing reduction on a poke trade you cannot finish.
tips.heading: Healing-cut finish

tips.text: If he rushes Frozen Heart, stop treating him as the same solo-kill target. Preserve farm and shorten attempts rather than forcing damage through the armor because the earlier lane felt easy.
tips.heading: Frozen Heart reassessment

tips.text: Leave Demonic Ascension's champion-drain range when your burst fails. The transformation can continue while he drains champions, so standing nearby waiting for your next rotation helps keep his ultimate active.
tips.heading: End the drain

tips.text: Pressure Swain in the side lane once your damage and healing reduction can win a short fight. If Frozen Heart or repeated drain still prevents a finish, clear the wave rather than extending the duel for another rotation.
tips.heading: Side-lane threshold

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield with Second Wind and Shield Bash. Choose Eclipse for shielded bruiser trades or Voltaic Cyclosword for burst when he has not built early armor.
itemization.heading: Sustain and first item

itemization.text: If Ignite is unavailable or insufficient, buy Executioner's Calling after your first completed item. Physical-damage Grievous Wounds helps limit his recovery without delaying your initial damage purchase.
itemization.heading: Healing reduction

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by shielding Seismic Shard poke, farming priority, and starting skirmishes with R while he cannot duel; Malphite wins extended armor fights and decides teamfights with Unstoppable Force.

keyTips.text: Shield his poke on cooldown. W his Seismic Shard as it flies, or shield Ground Slam and Thunderclap if he maxes those, so his mana buys him nothing.
keyTips.heading: Poke shield

keyTips.text: Do not take extended fights once armor lands. After his first armor buy your autos lose the stat race, so burst short and leave his Ground Slam attack-speed slow.
keyTips.heading: Armor refusal

keyTips.text: Play around his Granite Shield and mana. Trade when his rock shield is freshly broken and his mana runs low, because without either he is a mage with no spells.
keyTips.heading: Rock timing

tips.text: Take the free farm and priority. He cannot stop your push early, so crash waves and be first to skirmishes while he clears under turret.
tips.heading: Free priority

tips.text: Beware the turret dive bait. If you chase him under his turret he can clear the wave and let tower shots delete you, so dive only with your minions alive.
tips.heading: Turret bait

tips.text: Against AP Malphite, keep killing him. The AP build stays squishy, so punish every Shard trade with full combos instead of respecting armor that never comes.
tips.heading: AP punish

tips.text: After your first item, extended fights return. Lower cooldowns and sustain let you trade through his armor again, so retest the duel once Eclipse lands.
tips.heading: Item retest

tips.text: Your game is starting fights, not dueling him. R a carry to open skirmishes before Unstoppable Force ({cd:54:R}) picks your team, and force him to ult defensively.
tips.heading: Start first

tips.text: Win by out-moving him. He brings one teamfight ultimate; you bring repeated R picks and lane priority, so keep the map moving faster than his cooldown.
tips.heading: Tempo win

tips.text: Outscale his duel. Later, penetration plus sustain beats his armor stack, while his value stays locked to grouped ultimates your mobility can dodge or pre-empt.
tips.heading: Late duel

itemization.text: Build Eclipse first on the Conqueror line. Its shield and sustain carry the short trades, and later items reopen extended fights his armor tried to close.
Add Black Cleaver or Serylda's Grudge as armor stacks. Without penetration your mid-game combos bounce off, so buy shred before chasing more damage.
Start Doran's Shield with Flash and Teleport. Shield plus Second Wind erases Shard poke, and Teleport protects your priority if one Ground Slam trade goes wrong.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by farming well, keeping priority, and using her wave lead to help her jungler; Maokai wins when Flash-Twisted Advance or Nature's Grasp turns overextension into a gank.

keyTips.text: Use W against Bramble Smash when he steps up to trade. Absorb the Q damage rather than allowing repeated poke to erase the health you need for wave priority.
keyTips.heading: Shield the poke

keyTips.text: Before pushing beyond your safe retreat, account for Flash into Twisted Advance. His targeted root ({cd:57:W}) is a gank setup you cannot solve by merely sidestepping.
keyTips.heading: Flash root respect

keyTips.text: Prefer pushing and taking useful movement windows over holding a long freeze. Denying a few minions does less to stop his crowd control than getting yourself to the next fight first.
keyTips.heading: Push over freeze

tips.text: Maokai can absorb repeated pressure and still provide crowd control without much gold. Get ahead through waves and nearby skirmishes instead of spending the lane trying to kill through every Sap Magic heal.
tips.heading: Priority over solo kills

tips.text: If you want to punish Maokai directly, do it in the early levels before his defensive purchases. Do not expect the same solo-kill opportunity after he has reset and can sustain through your trades.
tips.heading: Early damage window

tips.text: Check his purchases before walking through Sapling Toss poke. A tank lane does not require the same respect for E damage as an AP build; do not carry that relaxed approach into magic-damage purchases.
tips.heading: AP sapling adjustment

tips.text: With safe priority and jungle information, proxy the wave to create time for an invade or gank. Cover the wave first so your movement produces an advantage beyond another low-value trade into his sustain.
tips.heading: Proxy into movement

tips.text: When Nature's Grasp is available, watch the route behind and beside your pushed wave. Do not let his advancing roots cut off your escape while you are busy hitting the next minion.
tips.heading: Ultimate gank angle

tips.text: Use the first move from your pushed wave to support your jungler when Maokai starts a nearby skirmish. Arriving early gives you a chance to answer his gank setup before his crowd control creates a numbers advantage.
tips.heading: Contest the setup

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield and build Eclipse for safe farming and shielded trades. Conqueror, Shield Bash, and Revitalize support the bruiser route while you keep the lane stable.
itemization.heading: Neutral lane start

itemization.text: Take Teleport and Ignite when you want to join nearby fights and threaten early healing trades. Ignite helps against Sap Magic, but do not let its availability tempt you to spend an entire wave chasing a sustained tank.
itemization.heading: Summoners for movement

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by playing around Fury, surviving the empowered Ruthless Predator, and outscaling into teamfights; a skilled Renekton wins lane outright and should be respected like a ban-level threat.

keyTips.text: Play around his Fury bar before anything else. Empowered Ruthless Predator destroys shields, so your W loses its usual value exactly when his bar is high.
keyTips.heading: Fury first

keyTips.text: Outspace him at level 1 with Q. Take W second to answer a Slice and Dice start, but expect good Renektons to hold W specifically to counter your shield.
keyTips.heading: Opening plan

keyTips.text: When he dashes forward near half Fury, dash away with Q immediately. He must then walk back on a spent dash or burn Fury chasing, and only then is W safe to block and punish with.
keyTips.heading: Dash discipline

tips.text: Without empowered W, you win trades. The lane flips entirely on whether his next Predator is empowered, so trade on his low-Fury windows only.
tips.heading: Low-Fury trades

tips.text: Remember Dominus ({cd:58:R}) refills his Fury instantly. A low bar stops being safety the moment his ultimate is available, so recheck before every trade after level 6.
tips.heading: Ult Fury

tips.text: Most Renekton picks are counterpick attempts rather than mains. Punish sloppy dash-ins and wasted Fury calmly instead of respecting every Renekton like an expert one.
tips.heading: Punish tourists

tips.text: Accept a lost lane against a truly skilled Renekton. Play safe, protect your health, and move your value into teamfights where your R pick outvalues his lane bullying.
tips.heading: Safe pivot

tips.text: Use your scaling. He falls off while your ultimate picks and mobility grow in fights, so every quiet minute after lane closes his window and opens yours.
tips.heading: Outscale plan

tips.text: Survive the empowered-W cycles without losing your health bar. A Renekton who never lands a shield-breaking stun on you has no kill pattern left.
tips.heading: Survive cycles

tips.text: Turn mid-game fights with R on his backline. He must walk into fights after his early dash pressure fades, while you choose the target and the moment.
tips.heading: Fight picks

itemization.text: Eclipse first on the Conqueror bruiser line. Extended low-Fury trades are your only winning pattern, and Eclipse plus Conqueror rewards staying in those fights.
An early Bramble Vest is a strong cheap buy here. It punishes his auto-heavy trades and trims his Cull the Meek healing while you survive lane.
Start Doran's Blade with Teleport and Flash. Blade supports the level-1 spacing duel, and Teleport is insurance against the one empowered combo that chunks you out of lane.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by shielding his entry, leaving before his attack-speed trade, and waiting out Stone Skin; Wukong wins long trades and level-6 knockup chains.

keyTips.text: W as Nimbus Strike reaches you, then E backward immediately. Shielding his E-Q burst and slowing his follow-up denies the attack-speed window he wants to spend on you.
keyTips.heading: Shield the entry

keyTips.text: Let Stone Skin stacks expire between trades. Reengaging while his passive armor and regeneration are still built up makes your next spell rotation much less effective.
keyTips.heading: Wait out armor

keyTips.text: Do not throw R at Wukong while Warrior Trickster ({cd:62:W}) is ready. Make him spend the clone first so your main engage is aimed at the real champion.
keyTips.heading: Hold the ultimate

tips.text: His E into Q requires a quick W answer. Keep trades tied to your available spells because his passive armor and repeated attacks reward every extra moment you stay beside him.
tips.heading: Fast defensive response

tips.text: During your retreat, hold Q if he still has Warrior Trickster available. Aim both Q casts after he uses W rather than dumping damage into the clone as he disengages.
tips.heading: Q after the clone

tips.text: Keep moving away while trading so he has to use Crushing Blow at reach instead of first landing an auto and resetting it with Q. That spacing removes an extra attack from his exchange.
tips.heading: Deny the reset auto

tips.text: At level 6, respect Cyclone and Ignite before dashing into him. The knockup can interrupt your dashes; do not assume a late movement command will get you out once the spin reaches you.
tips.heading: Level-6 restraint

tips.text: Against Grasp Q poke, use W as he steps in for Crushing Blow and answer with E if he follows using Nimbus Strike. This version of the lane calls for punishing his poke rather than starting an extended fight.
tips.heading: Grasp adjustment

tips.text: Remove Bone Plating with a light Q hit, then wait for its protection to end before spending your full burst. Do not combine his defensive rune and stacked Stone Skin into one expensive trade.
tips.heading: Bone Plating window

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and build Eclipse with Conqueror, Shield Bash, and Bone Plating. The shield helps answer his E-Q entry while your own Bone Plating reduces the opening burst.
itemization.heading: Bruiser start

itemization.text: Teleport and Ignite keep his lane trades punishable, but respect his own Ignite when judging an all-in. Avoid relying on sustain to survive his level-6 burst through healing reduction.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by contesting his unstacked opening, shielding Flamespitter, and leaving Overheat; Rumble wins if heat and Flash turn a short trade into an attack chase.

keyTips.text: If Rumble starts Electro Harpoon, contest the first wave with Q while dodging his shots. Do not assume every Rumble takes E first; identify his learned spell before forcing priority.
keyTips.heading: Level-1 priority

keyTips.text: From level 3, use W into Flamespitter damage, answer with Q, and slow him with E as you leave. Keep the exchange short instead of staying in his flame cone.
keyTips.heading: Shield the flame trade

keyTips.text: When his heat fills, E away from his empowered attacks. Overheat is a retreat signal even though he cannot freely cast more spells during it.
keyTips.heading: Overheat exit

tips.text: Rumble's heat state matters more than whether his last spell missed. Take brief spell trades, then create distance before his Overheat attacks can turn your retreat into a chase.
tips.heading: Heat controls the lane

tips.text: Before the second level-up, check how much heat Rumble has generated. Play beside your wave and give space if he can Overheat rather than letting his level-2 attacks catch you away from minion support.
tips.heading: Level-2 heat check

tips.text: Use an opening wave lead to reach level 3 first. That timing gives you W, E, and Q for a full short exchange instead of contesting him with only part of your kit.
tips.heading: Race the third level

tips.text: Do not stand close with your spells down when Rumble has Flash and Overheat available. If you lack Flash or Exhaust, keep enough distance that his instant approach cannot start an auto chase.
tips.heading: Flash plus heat

tips.text: After he resets, leave a low-health wave rather than overstaying for a few last hits. The Equalizer ({cd:68:R}) can catch your exit even when he is not close enough to start with an auto.
tips.heading: Do not linger after recall

tips.text: Use R to leave The Equalizer when its burning line cuts off your retreat. Save that option for the actual trap rather than spending your ultimate on a marginal trade and being stranded in the flames.
tips.heading: Ultimate escape

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield with Second Wind and Shield Bash, then build Eclipse. The start softens harpoon and flame poke; Eclipse adds a shield to your brief level-3-and-later trades.

itemization.text: Hexdrinker into Maw of Malmortius is useful when Rumble's magic damage is stopping you from collecting waves. Flash keeps your escape safer; Ignite is the riskier option for finishing an early lead.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by punishing missed Noxious Blasts and varying her entry around Miasma and Petrifying Gaze; Cassiopeia wins when poison and grounding keep her in Twin Fang range.

keyTips.text: After a few levels, engage when Noxious Blast misses or W its impact to start your response. Do not let the short base cooldown ({cd:69:Q}) turn your punish into a stationary extended trade.
keyTips.heading: Missed Q entry

keyTips.text: Track Miasma ({cd:69:W}) before committing forward. If she throws it at your feet, dash before it lands; once grounded, use your basic spells without their passive movement rather than repeatedly trying to dash.
keyTips.heading: Ground cooldown

keyTips.text: After R connects, use Q and move sideways or through her, then turn away before Petrifying Gaze lands. Avoid standing directly in front of her after your suppression finishes.
keyTips.heading: Post-R facing

tips.text: Play the first levels patiently, then use missed Q casts as openings. Your basic abilities still work without their passive dashes inside Miasma, but the loss of movement makes a long poisoned trade dangerous.
tips.heading: Grounding is manageable

tips.text: Use brushes and Doran's Shield to preserve health through the opening levels. Do not assume she started Twin Fang; a level-1 Noxious Blast start can punish an exposed first-wave approach.
tips.heading: Opening sustain

tips.text: If Noxious Blast hits, leave Twin Fang range instead of extending the punish. Twin Fang deals extra damage and heals against poisoned targets, so the trade changes sharply once Q poisons you.
tips.heading: Poisoned retreat

tips.text: During an all-in, vary your dashes across her position instead of repeatedly landing straight in front. Make her retarget both Noxious Blast and Petrifying Gaze rather than offering the same landing angle each time.
tips.heading: Unpredictable approach

tips.text: If you anticipate Petrifying Gaze, cast R before it lands to cover the impact with your unstoppable window. This requires a prediction; R cannot free you after the stun has already landed.
tips.heading: Predictive ultimate

tips.text: On the assassin build, disengage when a vital Q misses instead of forcing the rest of the all-in. Leaving with remaining mobility is better than waiting beside her for poisoned Twin Fangs while your damage is unavailable.
tips.heading: Failed burst exit

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield with Second Wind and Shield Bash. This supports the patient opening while W provides a shielded response when you step into Noxious Blast range.
itemization.heading: Ranged-lane start

itemization.text: Voltaic Cyclosword supports the burst route after level 6. Keep Flash and Teleport for safer attempts; the damage purchase does not replace playing around Miasma before your R engage.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by denying Siphoning Strike stacks without overpushing, surviving his level-6 all-in with dashes held, and peeling for carries late; Nasus wins after one jungle-assisted kill snowballs his stacks and turret.

keyTips.text: Deny stacks without shoving him to safety. Punish every Siphoning Strike walk-up with a short combo, but keep the wave on your side so he must overextend for gold.
keyTips.heading: Stack denial

keyTips.text: Hold dashes for Fury of the Sands. After level 6 his ultimate plus Wither runs you down, so kite the duration out and re-engage when it fades.
keyTips.heading: Ult kite

keyTips.text: Track the enemy jungler constantly. One death here hands him plates, stacks, and a turret, and the lane may never be winnable again.
keyTips.heading: Jungler track

tips.text: Play aggressive from level 1. He should not farm for free; every minion he takes without eating your combo is a stack you donated.
tips.heading: Early bully

tips.text: Respect Wither gank setups. His slow guarantees jungle arrival, so never trade deep without vision and a dash reserved for the escape.
tips.heading: Wither respect

tips.text: Adapt to poke Nasus starts. If he maxes Spirit Fire with Aery-style poke, Doran's Shield and shorter trades survive the chip he trades for stacks.
tips.heading: Poke adapt

tips.text: If you fall behind, peel for your carry. A stacked Nasus walks at your backline, and your R suppression plus slows protect the damage that kills him.
tips.heading: Peel duty

tips.text: Keep pressuring before his stacks spike. Crash waves and force fights while his ultimate is down, because quiet farming minutes are his win condition ticking.
tips.heading: Pressure clock

tips.text: Win by starving the stack clock. A Nasus behind on Siphoning Strike stacks cannot duel or threaten carries, and your team closes before he recovers.
tips.heading: Starve clock

tips.text: End fights before he becomes the raid boss. R his carries early and take objectives on your timing instead of letting him scale into grouped fights.
tips.heading: Early fights

itemization.text: Open Eclipse against his standard build or Voltaic Cyclosword to burst him. Eclipse wins the longer Wither trades; Voltaic punishes him before armor and stacks land.
Add Black Cleaver against his armor and health. Fast shred from your combos keeps your damage relevant while his stacks grow.
Start Doran's Shield against poke starts or Blade to bully stack starts, with Flash and Teleport. Match the start to his first ability, and keep Teleport for the reset after his ultimate chase.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by sidestepping Comet Spear, bursting before Aegis Assault blocks her, and outscaling his lane bullying; Pantheon wins early low-cooldown run-downs and decides other lanes with Grand Starfall.

keyTips.text: Sidestep Comet Spear above everything. Dodge or bait his Q, especially the thrown version, and punish its cooldown while his Mortal Will stacks are spent.
keyTips.heading: Spear dodge

keyTips.text: Burst before Aegis Assault. Land your damage before his shield faces you, because comboing into his E block feeds him a free winning trade.
keyTips.heading: Shield race

keyTips.text: Answer Shield Vault with your W. React or predict his stun jump with your shield, then trade back before his spear returns.
keyTips.heading: Vault answer

tips.text: Respect his level 1 and short spear cooldowns. He can run you down if you overextend early, so trade only at your spacing and top off health with potions.
tips.heading: Early respect

tips.text: Mind his execute spear. Empowered Comet Spear hits harder on low targets, so recall or potion before sitting in its lethal range.
tips.heading: Execute spear

tips.text: After level 6, ult him when his shield is spent. R onto him while Aegis Assault is down, or punish his cooldowns with your ultimate engage.
tips.heading: Six punish

tips.text: Track Grand Starfall ({cd:80:R}) after every death or reset. He returns to lane or another lane aiming his ultimate at someone, so ping and respect the sky.
tips.heading: Starfall track

tips.text: Outscale his bullying. Your duels and teamfights grow past his, so stop forcing lane kills and take fights where your R picks his carries.
tips.heading: Scale past

tips.text: Win by making spears whiff. Without Comet Spear hits he cannot stack pressure, and your scaling burst decides later fights on your engage.
tips.heading: Whiff scaling

tips.text: Punish his roams with plates and priority. When Grand Starfall takes him away, shove and take turret gold while he gambles on another lane.
tips.heading: Roam punish

itemization.text: Build Eclipse first on the Conqueror line. It sustains trades through his spear poke and shields the one Vault combo that lands.
Start Doran's Shield with Teleport and Flash. Shield survives spear spam, and Teleport recovers the lane after his early all-in pressure.
Add armor penetration as he builds bruiser. Without shred your mid-game bursts stop threatening him, so buy it before more raw damage.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by never eating Death's Grasp, taking short trades that deny his passive, and flashing his pull without hesitation; Mordekaiser stat-checks anyone he pulls and wins Realm of Death duels against targets who all-in too early.

keyTips.text: Never, ever get hit by Death's Grasp. Played cleanly you always win trades because he cannot start his stat-check without the pull landing.
keyTips.heading: Pull denial

keyTips.text: Take short trades that end before Darkness Rise spins up. Three hits is his whole fight plan, so your combo must be leaving before the aura and move speed activate.
keyTips.heading: Passive denial

keyTips.text: Flash his Death's Grasp without hesitating when low or after level 6 with cooldowns up. Eating the pull costs a heavy chunk or a death inside his ultimate, which is always worse than the Flash.
keyTips.heading: Flash the pull

tips.text: Use the bread-and-butter counter combo: W into him through his Obliterate, empowered auto, E to the side, then Q twice out while still dodging his pull.
tips.heading: Counter combo

tips.text: Play reactive before level 6. Do not walk into his Obliterate range to start trades yourself; wait for Death's Grasp to miss, then step in for a short combo and kite back out before his passive spins up.
tips.heading: Reactive start

tips.text: A single mistake can still kill you in an otherwise winning lane. Treat every pull cast as lethal and keep a dash reserved for it at all health totals.
tips.heading: One-mistake rule

tips.text: Try to dodge and cancel Realm of Death ({cd:82:R}) with your own R blink. It is difficult, but a cancelled ultimate leaves him without the stat steal his duel depends on.
tips.heading: Ult cancel

tips.text: Only all-in him below roughly a quarter health while his cooldowns are up. Above that line his ultimate plus Indestructible shield still wins the duel you started.
tips.heading: All-in line

tips.text: Win by making Death's Grasp whiff all game. Without pulls he never reaches you, and your short trades plus R picks decide every fight on your timing.
tips.heading: Whiff economy

tips.text: Force grouped fights over side-lane duels. His ultimate isolates one target, so fight where your team collapse answers the Realm of Death instead of feeding him isolated stats.
tips.heading: Group answer

itemization.text: Serpent's Fang is great when his team allows it, cutting his Indestructible shield in every trade; Maw of Malmortius is the fallback when you are struggling or facing double AP on top side.
Doran's Shield is the safe start for surviving his early Q poke, with Blade as the confident alternative. Match the start to how cleanly you trust your pull dodging.
Take Electrocute with Flash and Teleport. Burst trades end before his passive spins up, and Teleport protects you after the one pull that eventually lands.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by avoiding Mourning Mist and moving before Dark Procession closes; Yorick wins when the cage traps her for his summons and bruiser damage.

keyTips.text: Prioritize dodging Mourning Mist ({cd:83:E}). Do not spend your last dash moving toward Yorick when the mark can turn that approach into a losing trade.
keyTips.heading: Mist first

keyTips.text: Dash out of Dark Procession's forming area before the wall closes. Once trapped, do not rely on another short passive dash to solve the cage; keep Flash for a reliable emergency exit.
keyTips.heading: Move before the cage

keyTips.text: Use W as Yorick or his summons damage you, then hit him with the empowered return strike. Casting W too early wastes the damage-triggered increase you need in the close trade.
keyTips.heading: Shield real damage

tips.text: The lane is much easier while Yorick cannot pin you in Dark Procession. Contest the opening wave, then keep an exit available whenever you approach his E and W threat.
tips.heading: Cage discipline

tips.text: Play for level-1 priority with Q spacing. Hit Yorick from outside his Last Rites attack reach instead of exchanging autos to push the first wave.
tips.heading: Opening priority

tips.text: If Dark Procession catches you and Flash is unavailable, attack the destructible wall to open a way out. Recognize the cage as a separate target rather than continuing to attack Yorick inside it.
tips.heading: Break a trapped cage

tips.text: When fed, look for R onto Yorick after his Flash is spent. Commit the burst while he cannot Flash your engage rather than giving his bruiser build a long fight.
tips.heading: Lead into a pick

tips.text: Once Yorick has his bruiser items, retreat after spending Q and E even if you won the opening lane. His sustained damage can win the rematch while those spells are unavailable; do not stay in melee range trading autos.
tips.heading: Respect the bruiser rematch

tips.text: Keep the route out of his turret clear before pressuring him there. Without Flash, give up a close-range trade under his tower rather than risk Dark Procession trapping you in turret range.
tips.heading: Turret approach

itemization.text: Choose Doran's Blade if you can consistently dodge Mourning Mist; Doran's Shield is the safer alternative when his poke is denying farm. The aggressive start only pays if E does not keep marking you.
itemization.heading: Starting confidence

itemization.text: Build Eclipse for shielded exchanges and keep Flash to escape Dark Procession or dodge Mourning Mist. Ignite adds kill pressure, but it leaves less room for a failed cage dodge.
itemization.heading: First item and summoners

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins short Electrocute trades and level-6 picks; Kennen wins through free marks, extended poke, and a Slicing Maelstrom engage into her team.

keyTips.text: When Kennen walks too close, E into range, auto, and use both Q casts while moving back out. Leave after Electrocute rather than staying to trade into more marks.
keyTips.heading: Punish an overstep

keyTips.text: If you already carry a Mark of the Storm, move out before Electrical Surge can add another. Do not let his W turn a small poke hit into the start of a stun trade.
keyTips.heading: Marked retreat

keyTips.text: In grouped fights, catch Kennen before he starts Slicing Maelstrom or commit to killing his backline first. Do not spend the opening slowly trading into him while his ultimate reaches your carries.
keyTips.heading: Fight entry decision

tips.text: Whittle Kennen down without collecting free marks, then threaten R at level 6. Winning lane does not remove the danger of his ultimate reaching your backline at the next objective.
tips.heading: Lane versus teamfight

tips.text: Dodge Thundering Shuriken or W its impact when a dodge is unavailable. Keep his Q cooldown ({cd:85:Q}) in mind before stepping out for your next poke.
tips.heading: Shuriken answer

tips.text: Watch his W-empowered attack and avoid giving it a free hit. Electrocute and Ignite make that extra marked auto more dangerous than his ordinary last-hit harassment.
tips.heading: Empowered auto respect

tips.text: If he stays outside E reach, use W or a Q dash to close only far enough to land your short trade. Do not spend all your mobility reaching him and leave no route back out.
tips.heading: Bridge the spacing gap

tips.text: After short trades have lowered him, use level-6 R to start the kill attempt. Your new engage range is the reward for keeping enough health through his early poke.
tips.heading: Level-6 finish

tips.text: Avoid forcing a marginal turret dive just because Kennen is squishy. Slicing Maelstrom adds damage and marks in close range, making his turret much more dangerous than an ordinary ranged champion's.
tips.heading: Dive restraint

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield with Second Wind and Shield Bash. These cover his ranged harassment while your W creates the shielded return hit for a short Electrocute trade.
itemization.heading: Poke sustain

itemization.text: Build Voltaic Cyclosword for burst into his low defenses. If both enemy top-side threats deal heavy magic damage, Hexdrinker into Maw of Malmortius gives a safer route through his level-6 pressure.
itemization.heading: Damage or magic defense

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by shielding every Decisive Strike, never eating Judgment for free, and engaging only when his defensive cooldowns are spent; Garen wins silence trades and teamfight executions on your carries.

keyTips.text: Always have W ready for his Decisive Strike. Shielding the silence hit is the whole matchup; without W up, stay out of its reach entirely.
keyTips.heading: Silence shield

keyTips.text: Read his level 1 from his keystone. Conqueror means respect Judgment spin at level 1 and match carefully with W, while Phase Rush points to a Decisive Strike start you can space with Q.
keyTips.heading: Level-1 read

keyTips.text: Answer his Q into E combo with W then instant E out. Cancelling your W dash with E after the cast beats the silence, because a dash already cast is not stopped by it.
keyTips.heading: Combo escape

tips.text: Never let him spin on you unanswered when W is down. Judgment ({cd:86:E}) without a shield trade is free damage he repeats all lane.
tips.heading: Spin respect

tips.text: Engage only into spent cooldowns: his W shield down, or both Q and E down. Trading into Courage ({cd:86:W}) wastes your burst on his damage reduction window.
tips.heading: Engage check

tips.text: You are generally stronger in lane, so press the health bar while respecting the one combo. Small wins stack because his passive sustain needs time out of combat to work.
tips.heading: Lane press

tips.text: Commit to the bruiser build to keep beating him past lane. Eclipse into Death's Dance style durability keeps your trades winning when pure burst stops finishing him.
tips.heading: Bruiser commit

tips.text: Track his R in teamfights. A silenced Ambessa caught near his execute range dies before dashing, so enter fights after Decisive Strike and Demacian Justice ({cd:86:R}) have targets that are not you.
tips.heading: Execute watch

tips.text: Win the W-for-Q exchange every cycle. If your shield always eats his silence engage, he has no way to start a trade you lose.
tips.heading: Cycle control

tips.text: Carry the lane lead into fights on your R. Suppress backline targets he cannot reach without Flash, and force him to run through your team to matter.
tips.heading: Backline access

itemization.text: Build Eclipse first. Its burst proc plus shield fits the shield-for-silence trade, where your W eats his Decisive Strike and Eclipse procs as you hit back, and it scales into the bruiser items this matchup demands later.
Add Death's Dance and an armor-penetration slot as he stacks health and armor from Courage. Without penetration your mid-game trades bounce off his passive resistances.
Start Doran's Blade with Flash and Teleport. You are the stronger laner, so Blade funds the press, and Teleport protects the lead if one silence trade goes wrong.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by countering Riven engages with W, keeping a disengage after every combo, and fighting her spent-shield windows; Riven wins levels 1 to 2, full-combo races, and the cooldown war after a failed all-in.

keyTips.text: Do not only space her with Q. Play surprisingly aggressive with W: when she jumps on you, shielding her engage and hitting back is how trades flip.
keyTips.heading: Counter W

keyTips.text: Always keep a way out. If your full combo does not kill her, her shorter cooldowns finish you, so all-in only with lethal confirmed.
keyTips.heading: Exit rule

keyTips.text: Trade after her Valor shield fades or bait it out first. Electrocute burst through a spent shield is your cleanest short-trade window.
keyTips.heading: Shield window

tips.text: Respect levels 1 and 2 and her level-up timers. You start winning from level 3, so give early waves rather than gambling the lane before your kit is complete.
tips.heading: Early respect

tips.text: Win by countering, not by engaging. Your best trades start with her Broken Wings spent into your W, not with your dashes spent into her stun.
tips.heading: Counter plan

tips.text: Do not let her proxy. The moment she spends abilities on the wave behind you, send R at her and punish the cooldown-free target.
tips.heading: Proxy punish

tips.text: Fear her Eclipse spike in extended fights. Even in a learned matchup her first-item all-in bursts through sloppy spacing, so keep trades short around it.
tips.heading: Eclipse spike

tips.text: Use Exhaust value through her ultimate combo. It stalls her burst long enough for your cooldowns to return and turns her all-in into your turn.
tips.heading: Exhaust turn

tips.text: Protect an early lead ruthlessly. Ahead, your counter-trades bully her every engage, while an even lane leaves her scaling and cooldown edge live.
tips.heading: Lead protection

tips.text: Force fights where her proxy and side-lane cooldown games do not matter. Your R suppression starts the fight she must answer without a wave to play through.
tips.heading: Fight forcing

itemization.text: Eclipse first mirrors her spike with shield and burst for counter-trades, and Death's Dance follows to survive the one full combo you fail to space.
Serpent's Fang is the situational slot when her Valor shields and Eclipse procs keep eating your burst. Cutting shields restores your short-trade lethal math.

Start Doran's Blade with Flash and Exhaust. Blade's early attack damage powers your level-3 trades, where you shield her Broken Wings engage with W and hit back with an Electrocute combo; Exhaust is taken to blunt her ultimate all-in rather than for lane poke.
