guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by dodging Shadow Dash, refusing trades into his empowered autos, and punishing every Stand United with plates; Shen wins extended fist fights and outnumbers your team across the map.

keyTips.text: Dodge or shield Shadow Dash before anything else. Dash sideways or tank the taunt with W, because the taunt into empowered autos is his only real kill threat.
keyTips.heading: Taunt answer

keyTips.text: Never trade into his Twilight Assault autos. When his blade passes through you and his autos glow, leave; those empowered hits win every extended trade.
keyTips.heading: Empowered refusal

keyTips.text: Burst short and leave. Quick Electrocute-style combos that end before he drags his blade through you are how you win a lane you can never fist-fight.
keyTips.heading: Short bursts

tips.text: Treat it as a farm lane you slowly win. He has no all-in without jungle help, so take clean bursts, keep your health high, and recall rather than dying to a gank at low health.
tips.heading: Farm control

tips.text: If he takes Ignite, play safer early. Ignite Shen is trading real kill pressure for his late map play, so survive it and punish him with your Teleport advantage on resets.
tips.heading: Ignite read

tips.text: Punish health-over-armor starts. If he builds health before armor, your combos keep winning; armor first is the signal to shorten trades and play for plates.
tips.heading: Build read

tips.text: Every Stand United ({cd:98:R}) is free plates. The moment he ults away, hard-shove and take turret gold with Demolish while he saves someone across the map.
tips.heading: Ult plates

tips.text: Abuse his weak waveclear to move first. Crash the wave, then proxy or dive mid while he is stuck clearing under his turret without his ultimate.
tips.heading: First move

tips.text: Win the map trade: his ultimate saves one teammate, your pressure takes plates and turrets. Keep shoving before objectives so he must choose between his turret and his team.
tips.heading: Map trade

tips.text: In fights, R his carries through his protection. Serpent's Fang value grows when he shields allies with Stand United and items, so burst the target his shield cannot save in time.
tips.heading: Shield burst

itemization.text: Build Eclipse first on the Conqueror line. Longer trades stack Conqueror while Eclipse shield covers the one taunt combo you fail to dodge.
Add Serpent's Fang when his team stacks shields beyond him. It cuts his Ki Barrier and ally shields alike, and it becomes mandatory with other shielders on his team.

Start Doran's Blade with Teleport and Flash, and take Demolish plus Bone Plating in Resolve. Blade funds early bursts, Teleport matches his map play, and Demolish converts every ultimate he spends into turret gold.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins through minion cover, short shielded trades, and punishes without True Grit stacks; Graves wins when she fights his stacked defenses or gets caught by wall-accelerated Q damage.

keyTips.text: Keep minions between you and Graves so they absorb his shotgun attacks. Step around the wave only when your trade is ready instead of giving him free direct shots while farming.
keyTips.heading: Minion screen

keyTips.text: Leave the return explosion of End of the Line, and avoid standing beside terrain that makes it detonate sooner. A dash timed for an open-lane Q may be too late when he fires into a nearby wall.
keyTips.heading: Q away from walls

keyTips.text: Prefer an all-in when his Quickdraw armor stacks have expired. Do not treat the base E cooldown ({cd:104:E}) as proof the stacks are gone; watch the active defenses before committing.
keyTips.heading: Empty armor window

tips.text: Treat Graves as a burst-heavy duelist rather than a fragile ranged target. His armor stacks and build choices change the kill threshold, and even a gank does not make an extended melee fight safe.
tips.heading: Respect the ranged bruiser

tips.text: If Graves starts Quickdraw with Flash and Ignite, respect the early chase. Preserve minion cover rather than contesting an exposed auto trade into his E start.
tips.heading: Level-1 restraint

tips.text: W an incoming shotgun attack, return an auto, and Q backward. Finish the short exchange without remaining beside him for another round of direct shots.
tips.heading: Shielded exit

tips.text: Keep Quickdraw available in your damage estimate when lining up Sundering Slam. If Graves still has E, avoid committing Q2 to an easy straight-line target he can dash away from.
tips.heading: Q2 aim check

tips.text: If he follows your retreat, E him to slow the chase and line up Q2. Let his forward movement bring him into your damage rather than using every dash to chase his Quickdraw.
tips.heading: Chase reversal

tips.text: After your first spell rotation in a 1v2, leave direct shotgun range while your cooldowns recover. Graves can still burst one of you down; extra allies do not remove the need for short trades.
tips.heading: Do not overstay a gank

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield with Second Wind and Shield Bash, then build Eclipse. The sustain helps you keep farming behind minions, while the first-item shield supports the brief W-auto-Q response.
itemization.heading: Start for poke

itemization.text: Use Black Cleaver on the bruiser route or Serylda's Grudge on the penetration route when you need side-lane damage through his armor. Check whether he chose bruiser, crit, or Bloodthirster before judging his durability.
itemization.heading: Armor answer

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by collecting his shove, spacing Thundering Smash, and resetting between Frenzied Maul marks; Volibear wins extended trades and low-health turret dives.

keyTips.text: From level 3, poke with Q while staying outside Thundering Smash reach. His Q stun sets up Sky Splitter; retreat before he reaches you and W the lightning damage if escape is too late.
keyTips.heading: Deny the stun setup

keyTips.text: Do not reengage while Frenzied Maul has you marked. Wait for the mark to disappear rather than giving him a stronger second W and its heal; the cast cooldown is {cd:106:W}.
keyTips.heading: Wait out the mark

keyTips.text: If he dives with Stormbringer, use your own R to buy time during the turret disable. This is an emergency stall, so recall before low health makes his next dive easy.
keyTips.heading: Dive stall

tips.text: Let his passive push the wave into you when you cannot contest. Tank Volibear becomes easier to handle with items, while an AP bruiser build remains a reason to clear side waves and join fights.
tips.heading: Collect and scale

tips.text: If he starts E, take only a light Q trade before the first waves meet and his passive stacks. Dodge Sky Splitter with your Q dash rather than standing in the circle to contest an auto.
tips.heading: Opening before stacks

tips.text: When your opening Q is on cooldown, give up priority and collect his crash. Do not turn the wave contest into an auto battle that lets his passive and repeated W casts take over.
tips.heading: Concede the crash

tips.text: Against AP bruiser Volibear, push the side wave before objectives and group. Do not assume a lane lead lets you beat the sustained damage of that build in a long duel.
tips.heading: Build-dependent side lane

tips.text: When his passive clears the wave, check whether he walks into your jungle or toward mid. Warn those lanes immediately instead of treating every free incoming wave as a harmless farming trade.
tips.heading: Track his shove exits

tips.text: Against tank Volibear, preserve even farm until your items let you take stronger Q trades. Keep the fights brief even then; scaling past his tank build does not make repeated marked W hits acceptable.
tips.heading: Tank build transition

itemization.text: Start Doran's Shield and build Eclipse for AD, haste, and a shield in your short exchanges. Conqueror with Shield Bash and Revitalize supports this setup without requiring you to stay for his second W.
itemization.heading: Shielded trades

itemization.text: Keep Flash for safety and add Executioner's Calling when his repeat W healing becomes a problem. Apply physical damage before his healing trade rather than expecting your W shield to prevent his recovery.
itemization.heading: Healing answer

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by fighting beside her wave, shielding his leap, and delaying burst through Battle Roar; Rengar wins early extended trades and heals back an impatient full rotation.

keyTips.text: After level 3, W his Q-enhanced leap onto you, then E to slow him and line up both Q casts. Keep the exchange brief rather than staying beside his attack-speed buff.
keyTips.heading: Leap response

keyTips.text: Do not spend every damage spell immediately after he lands. Battle Roar heals recent damage, so keep part of your burst until he has used W instead of giving him one large amount to recover.
keyTips.heading: Delay the burst

keyTips.text: Stand close to your minions when Rengar wants the first-level fight. Make a leap cost him wave damage instead of meeting his Q attacks alone beside the brush.
keyTips.heading: Level-1 wave cover

tips.text: Respect his early Q damage and fight from a position where your wave can punish a jump. Your response needs both a fast shield and enough restraint to avoid handing all your burst back through W healing.
tips.heading: Short retaliation

tips.text: Ward the lane brush on your way into lane when you need warning of his opening leap. Do not walk past an unchecked brush and rely on reacting only after he has already started his level-1 attack.
tips.heading: Opening brush vision

tips.text: End the exchange while you still have a retreat spell. His early cooldowns, attack speed, and sustain favor the extended fight, so do not follow another brush leap with your own spells already spent.
tips.heading: Shorter cooldown respect

tips.text: If he is low, watch the minions he can jump to while escaping through brush. Aim R at a predictable landing when the catch is clear instead of following his jumps with every basic dash.
tips.heading: Predict the exit jump

tips.text: With Executioner's Calling, land physical damage before his Battle Roar heal. Keep healing reduction active during the trade rather than waiting to hit him only after he has recovered the recent burst.
tips.heading: Cut the recovery

tips.text: Before spending your final movement on a low-health Rengar, account for Thrill of the Hunt. His camouflage and movement can end the chase, so use a clear R catch rather than running blind after his escape.
tips.heading: Ultimate escape check

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade into Voltaic Cyclosword and buy Executioner's Calling to contest his healing. Plated Steelcaps helps against his repeated attacks when staying healthy in lane is the priority.

itemization.text: Against lethality Rengar, consider Death's Dance second or third to soften his physical burst. Keep the short-trade approach against bruiser builds rather than assuming the same item timing answers both styles.
itemization.heading: Lethality response

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by denying Vitals with dashes, shielding her Lunge, and snowballing before Ravenous Hydra; Fiora outscales the side-lane duel and punishes every dash spent into her.

keyTips.text: Keep W ready as counteroffense. When she lunges with Q, shield the Lunge and retaliate with a full combo instead of running first.
keyTips.heading: Lunge answer

keyTips.text: Kite around her passive Vitals with your dashes and keep the fight inside your wave. Minion aggro plus denied Vitals is how her trade math collapses.
keyTips.heading: Vital denial

keyTips.text: Block the last Grand Challenge Vital by dashing to a wall. Hugging terrain makes one Vital unreachable and denies her healing zone.
keyTips.heading: Wall block

tips.text: If you play aggressive at level 1, do not dash in, and you must land Q2. Dashing straight into Fiora lets her proc Vitals and run you down before your cooldowns come back.
tips.heading: Level-1 rule

tips.text: Playing passive until level 3 is a valid fallback. From level 3 your full kit starts winning the shield-and-dash trades.
tips.heading: Level-3 start

tips.text: Abuse her weak early waveclear for tempo. Crash waves she cannot thin quickly, and punish her for stepping to the wave without respecting your casters.
tips.heading: Wave tempo

tips.text: Slow down hard once she completes Ravenous Hydra. She sustains off the wave between trades, so short winning trades stop sticking unless you commit fully.
tips.heading: Hydra respect

tips.text: Side-lane dueling her late is a losing default. She outscales the 1v1, so take your lead into grouped fights where your R suppression decides targets faster.
tips.heading: Leave the duel

tips.text: Snowball the lane before her sustain item lands. Early priority, plates and a health lead let you leave the side lane and suppress enemy carries with R in grouped fights, where she cannot duel you one by one.
tips.heading: Early snowball

tips.text: Win fights, not the split. Suppress a carry with R and force her to teamfight on your timing instead of scaling alone in a side lane.
tips.heading: Fight plan

itemization.text: Delay anti-heal until it matters: after your first item, or once her Ravenous Hydra lands. Executioner's Calling bought too early slows your own spike without a sustain target to cut.
Match the start to her keystone: Doran's Shield into Grasp or Press the Attack poke, Doran's Blade into Conqueror duelists. The wrong start gives away the level-1 priority fight.
Choose Eclipse for bruiser duels or Voltaic Cyclosword for burst trades. Either way the first item must land before her sustain turns trades into a healing race you lose.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins only by never letting Darius start auto trades, answering his casts with dashes, and scaling toward his backline; Darius wins any trade he starts and every extended bleed fight.

keyTips.text: Whoever engages first loses. Never jump onto Darius without a reason; a wasted engage costs you Flash or your life.
keyTips.heading: First-move rule

keyTips.text: Space him at level 1 with Q at max reach. Land two Q casts without eating a single auto before you think about walking closer.
keyTips.heading: Level-1 spacing

keyTips.text: Cap his autos with your passive-empowered attack spacing. He should get at most one auto, or only a W hit, before you are out of reach again.
keyTips.heading: Auto cap

tips.text: If he casts Decimate, Q away from the blade arc. If he pulls you with Apprehend ({cd:122:E}), you can win the moment: W into him, Q back out, and keep E as the final escape with its slow.
tips.heading: Cast answers

tips.text: Beware a Phase Rush level-1 run-down. Give the first wave respect if he sprints at you, since early bleed stacks plus the speed proc can chase you out of lane.
tips.heading: Rush respect

tips.text: Play losing lane gracefully if he gets ahead. Not dying matters more than cs here; ping your team off fights near him and give waves you cannot safely touch.
tips.heading: Lose gracefully

tips.text: If lane is lost, stop dueling him and build for burst: Voltaic Cyclosword into Serylda's Grudge, then use R to reach his bot-lane carries in fights instead of fighting a fed Darius in the side lane.
tips.heading: Backline pivot

tips.text: Only revisit the 1v1 on the bruiser build once your items land. Eclipse plus durability lets you survive five stacks long enough for your shorter cooldowns to win the rematch.
tips.heading: Bruiser rematch

tips.text: Starve his bleed. Every trade where he ends below five stacks is a trade your burst already won, so disengage before Hemorrhage maxes and Noxian Guillotine ({cd:122:R}) threatens.
tips.heading: Stack starvation

tips.text: Win through his team, not through him. Suppress a carry with R and let your team collapse while Darius walks at the fight without a dash to close distance.
tips.heading: Team pivot

itemization.text: Choose the first item by his build. Eclipse bruiser answers his standard bruiser setup in longer fights, while Voltaic Cyclosword burst is the pick into a Phase Rush build that cannot afford to be bursted first.
Doran's Blade is the confident start for solo-kill pressure; Doran's Shield is the safe start when you expect to lose early trades. Match the start to how you plan to play level 1.
Take Electrocute with Flash and Ignite plus Bone Plating. Burst trades are your only winning pattern, Ignite cuts his Decimate healing, and Bone Plating blunts the pull combo.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by shielding his hammer burst, landing damage before Thundering Blow knocks her away, and all-inning his ranged form; Jayce wins spacing duels and punishes every missed dash.

keyTips.text: Shield his hammer combo, dodge his cannon shots. Block melee To the Skies burst with W, and sidestep or W his ranged Shock Blast so neither form pokes you for free.
keyTips.heading: Form answers

keyTips.text: Get your damage out before Thundering Blow. His hammer E knocks you away and cancels dashes, so burst first and keep a dash for after the knockback.
keyTips.heading: Knockback race

keyTips.text: All-in only his ranged form. Right after he transforms to cannon he is most vulnerable for a few seconds, with no knockback ready to peel you.
keyTips.heading: Form window

tips.text: Play defensively and let him push. He must snowball to matter, while you outscale hard, so trade only when he forces a trade onto you.
tips.heading: Safe scaling

tips.text: Use the simple repeat combo: E in, empowered auto, Q out. It procs your burst before his knockback and never leaves you standing in his hammer range.
tips.heading: Repeat combo

tips.text: Beware fog-of-war poke. Shock Blast casts from brush chunk you before you see him, so ward lane brush and respect cannon range when he disappears.
tips.heading: Fog respect

tips.text: Chilling until level 6 is a winning line. At 6 your R gives you the all-in his kit cannot peel if you predict Thundering Blow and blink through it.
tips.heading: Six timing

tips.text: Never overdash forward without lethal. If your combo leaves him alive, his shorter cooldowns and chase run you down, so confirm the kill before spending everything.
tips.heading: Lethal check

tips.text: Win by outscaling his lane kingdom. Even trades crown you later, because lethality Ambessa one-shots the carries his poke only softens.
tips.heading: Scale crown

tips.text: Force fights where his spacing breaks. R through his knockback onto his team denies his peel, and grouped fights punish a champion built to duel at range.
tips.heading: Peel denial

itemization.text: Rush Voltaic Cyclosword on the lethality line. Its slow sticks you to a champion whose whole defense is knockback spacing, and your dashes charge it constantly.
Start Doran's Shield with Flash and Teleport. Shield plus Second Wind survives cannon poke, and Teleport protects you if a hammer trade knocks you out of lane.
Take Shield Bash and Second Wind in Resolve. Shield Bash rewards every blocked Shock Blast, and Second Wind patches the poke between your short combos.

keyTips.text: Never spend dashes forward without an exit. A good Gnar saves Hop to chase your engage, so engaging dashless turns your trade into his run-down.

keyTips.text: Respect Mega Gnar near walls completely. Dodge his smashes and stuns, and never stand between him and terrain when his ultimate can pin you.

tips.text: Accept the farm matchup. If he plays well neither of you dies, so take Electrocute pokes, finish him when low, and scale instead of forcing.

tips.text: Time W into his Hyper proc. When two rings sit on you, shield the third-hit burst or leave before his passive speed lets him chase.

tips.text: Hit your Q2 or do not trade. Your second Q is the damage that makes pokes stick; careful aim matters more here than combo speed.

tips.text: Play much safer after his Trinity Force. His kiting and damage jump at the spike, but you outscale him later, so survive the item window.

tips.text: Punish tiny mistakes hard. One overstep in Mini form eats your full combo; the same patience protects you, because his punishment for your overstep is just as fast.

tips.text: Win by outscaling his lane. Patience and clean pokes bring you to fights where your R picks outvalue his form-dependent engage.

tips.text: Force fights on Mini Gnar timing. When Mega fades he cannot teamfight, so start with R before his Rage rebuilds.

Start Doran's Shield with Teleport and Flash. Shield survives boomerang poke while you farm to your spike, and Teleport covers a Mega Gnar trade gone wrong.
Take Shield Bash and Second Wind in Resolve. Shield Bash rewards blocked boomerangs, and Second Wind patches his poke between your trades.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins by denying blob pickups, spacing Stretching Strikes, and preserving cooldowns for a revive; Zac wins through sustain, surprise slingshots, and an overcommit into Cell Division.

keyTips.text: Step or dash onto Zac's dropped chunks before he collects them. Denying those pickups prevents part of his repeat-trade healing without requiring you to chase him for another full exchange.
keyTips.heading: Deny the blobs

keyTips.text: If Zac hits a minion with Stretching Strikes, move out before he attacks you as the second target. The initial skillshot aimed away from you can still become the setup for pulling both targets together.
keyTips.heading: Minion Q warning

keyTips.text: Before triggering Cell Division, check whether you will have enough damage left for the bloblets. Do not exhaust your spells for the first health bar and then die beside him after he recombines.
keyTips.heading: Revive budget

tips.text: His first defensive recall makes a solo kill harder, so farm cleanly and deny the healing you can reach. Do not spend every ability triggering Cell Division unless you can also finish its bloblets safely.
tips.heading: Sustain before kills

tips.text: Dodge Stretching Strikes' initial line when it is aimed directly at you. If you cannot avoid the hit, W the damage rather than expecting the shield to prevent its crowd control.
tips.heading: First Q dodge

tips.text: Your best direct kill opportunity is before his first defensive purchases. Take a clean early trade when available, but do not keep forcing the same finish after his first recall has made his sustain harder to overcome.
tips.heading: Early kill window

tips.text: Check fog near his turret before walking forward to pressure it. Zac can prepare Elastic Slingshot out of sight and turn your approach into a turret-side ambush.
tips.heading: Hidden slingshot

tips.text: At close range, W an Elastic Slingshot landing you cannot dash away from. Absorbing the damage is the fallback; the shield does not stop the knockup from connecting.
tips.heading: Close landing shield

tips.text: Keep landing Q sweet spots against his health build instead of spending the whole fight chasing chunks. Your percentage-health damage is the pressure that makes denying a nearby blob worthwhile.
tips.heading: Sweet-spot damage

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and build Eclipse with Conqueror, Shield Bash, and Revitalize. This supports sustained lane stability and shielded responses without making a post-recall solo kill mandatory.
itemization.heading: Bruiser setup

itemization.text: Buy Executioner's Calling to limit blob healing and consider Mortal Reminder later for healing reduction with armor penetration. Ignite can help an early finish, but it does not replace saving damage for Cell Division.
itemization.heading: Healing reduction

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins with one-sided short trades, W answers to Tactical Sweep, and R used to ruin Hookshot engages; Camille wins extended auto trades and the Trinity Force all-in.

keyTips.text: Never stand in the outer half of Tactical Sweep. Answer it with W into an empowered auto and E away before she follows up.
keyTips.heading: Sweep answer

keyTips.text: Hit without being hit back. Kite her Precision Protocol autos with E and save Q to disengage or dodge Hookshot instead of starting trades with it.
keyTips.heading: One-sided trades

keyTips.text: Hold R as a Hookshot answer. Cast it as she launches off the wall, or pre-aim it at the anchor point she first dashes toward, to buffer through the engage.
keyTips.heading: R buffer

tips.text: Levels 1 to 3 are volatile and can decide the lane. Fight for the middle of the lane and take clean short trades rather than conceding the wave for free.
tips.heading: Opening levels

tips.text: Use the E auto into Q exit pattern so she does not get even a single answering auto. Every free auto she lands feeds her passive shield and turns the trade.
tips.heading: Clean exit

tips.text: Later in lane, Q into Q poke is safe chip. It pressures her health bar without giving her the extended auto fight she wants.
tips.heading: Q poke

tips.text: Respect the Trinity Force spike. If you are even when she completes it, her burst and all-in threat jump, so stop forcing trades you were winning earlier.
tips.heading: Trinity spike

tips.text: Keep refusing extended fights after level 6. Her Hextech Ultimatum ({cd:164:R}) locks you into exactly the long duel your kit loses, so trade short and leave before it comes down.
tips.heading: Ultimatum refusal

tips.text: Bank a lead before her first full item, then protect it. The lane is decided early; an even game at Trinity Force hands her the all-in timing.
tips.heading: Early bank

tips.text: Scale with your R ranks in later fights. Your suppression pick on a carry decides teamfights while she must find a clean Ultimatum target, so group on your ultimate cooldown.
tips.heading: Pick fights

itemization.text: Open with Serpent's Fang. It cuts through her Adaptive Defenses shield in every short trade, and it keeps paying off if she later adds Sterak's Gage or her team stacks shields.
Take Teleport and Ignite with Doran's Blade. Ignite pressures the early volatile levels where the lane is decided, while Teleport covers you if a Hookshot trade goes wrong.
If her team leans on shielding beyond Camille, keep Serpent's Fang as a permanent slot rather than a lane-only buy. Its value grows with every shield she and her allies stack.

guides.favoredWhen: Ambessa wins through minion cover, spaced Q sweet spots, and a saved dash for Abyssal Dive; Tahm Kench wins repeated autos, healing Tongue Lashes, and turret-side Devour catches.

keyTips.text: Do not feed Tongue Lash to a low-health Tahm Kench. Dodge or use minion cover rather than assuming W shielding the damage also prevents his champion-hit healing.
keyTips.heading: Low-health Tongue Lash

keyTips.text: Always retain one dash for Abyssal Dive. E can slow his auto chase, but spending every movement to poke leaves you trapped when the W landing circle appears, including from fog of war.
keyTips.heading: Keep a dive dodge

keyTips.text: Back away before repeated hits build An Acquired Taste near his turret. Do not let him Devour you and reposition the fight under his tower just to land one more Q.
keyTips.heading: Devour near his tower

tips.text: Use Q sweet spots to wear down his health while denying repeated attacks. His apparent tankiness is not permission to stand beside him: autos build the stacks that unlock Devour.
tips.heading: Space the health tank

tips.text: Farm behind your minions so they intercept Tongue Lash ({cd:223:Q}). Keep your spacing when he walks around the wave; do not concede free Grasp attacks to maintain a last-hit position.
tips.heading: Minion screen

tips.text: Hit your Q sweet spots and W the damage you cannot avoid while circling back out. Short spell trades exploit his health build without entering the extended auto fight he wants.
tips.heading: Spaced damage

tips.text: If Abyssal Dive begins while he is within your R line, interrupt him with Public Execution before he disappears. Your R can also buffer an incoming stun, but it is not a cleanse after you are already disabled.

tips.text: When he invests in Heartsteel, keep playing through Q sweet spots rather than matching his autos. His health-heavy purchase gives your percentage-health damage a clearer target as your own items arrive.
tips.heading: Heartsteel transition

tips.text: Before committing to a carry in a teamfight, account for Tahm Kench's allied Devour. He can remove your target and return them with a shield, so do not assume the first low-health carry is an immediate kill.
tips.heading: Devour peel check

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and choose Eclipse for shielded bruiser exchanges or Voltaic Cyclosword for burst. Both approaches still depend on landing Q at the right range instead of trading autos.

itemization.text: Consider Serpent's Fang when Tahm Kench has other shielders alongside him or you intend to attack the backline he protects. The anti-shield effect is useful against allied Devour shielding as well as his own Thick Skin.
itemization.heading: Shielding answer

keyTips.text: Punish after Blood Frenzy ends and before the next W ({cd:233:W}). Do not waste that opening waiting until she can restart the attack-speed chase.

keyTips.text: Use R to avoid or punish Chilling Scream after she commits the channel. Do not stand between her and a nearby wall waiting for the fully charged knockback.
keyTips.heading: Scream punishment

tips.text: Do not match Briar's frenzied autos head-on. Use the wave behind you, then trade back while Blood Frenzy and Chilling Scream are unavailable rather than while her defensive channel is active.
tips.heading: Punish the downtime

tips.text: If Briar starts Head Rush with Press the Attack, a W start with Electrocute and Shield Bash lets you answer the opening burst. Respect her learned Q instead of assuming she must begin with frenzy.
tips.heading: Level-1 Q check

tips.text: Use your health potion early enough to enter the next trade healthy. Snack Attack deals more damage based on your missing health, so delaying the potion until her next bite makes the chase more dangerous.

tips.text: Do not dump your remaining burst into a charging Chilling Scream. The channel reduces damage and heals Briar; move out and spend your damage after that protection ends.
tips.heading: Channel damage reduction

tips.text: Keep your ordinary dashes available to leave Chilling Scream's line before release. When R is unavailable, move across the scream rather than backing toward the wall it can slam you into.
tips.heading: Wall-safe movement

tips.text: If Briar left lane without a lead, pressure her in teamfights before Certain Death connects. She is more vulnerable without the additional defenses and sustain from a successful ultimate.
tips.heading: Fight without her R stats

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade and build Eclipse. The extra short-trade shield supports the jump response while you use E and Q to leave her attack range.
itemization.heading: Shielded bruiser start

itemization.text: Take Electrocute, Shield Bash, and Bone Plating with Flash and Ignite. This setup pays for a brief retaliatory trade and protects her opening contact instead of asking you to stay through Blood Frenzy.

keyTips.text: Make mounted Kled spend Violent Tendencies before engaging. Its fourth attack carries the large damage hit, so do not volunteer to take the end of his W while trying to finish a short trade.

keyTips.text: Save your kill burst for dismounted Kled with W unavailable ({cd:240:W}). Entering while Violent Tendencies is ready gives him fast courage gains and a chance to remount through your damage.

tips.text: Treat dismount as a reset in your decision, not as the final part of one chase. Recover your cooldowns, check Violent Tendencies, and only then decide whether you can burst him before courage restores Skaarl.

tips.text: At level 3, do not assume Kled has wasted W just because you have not seen it trigger. He can delay learning Violent Tendencies and put the point in when you finally commit.
tips.heading: Unlearned W trap

tips.text: Keep early exchanges brief when your jungler is elsewhere. Losing health to mounted Kled gives his strong tower dive and Ignite a much easier target, even if you never intended to all-in him.

tips.text: If he casts Q and E before dismounting, do not chase straight after Skaarl leaves. The remaining Bear Trap tether can still pull you back while dismounted Kled builds courage.

tips.text: Keep a dash available during the dismounted kill attempt. Pocket Pistol knocks Kled backward and restores courage, so do not use your last movement just to reach his initial position.

tips.text: If Kled remounts, end the pursuit rather than fighting the restored health and refreshed mounted Q and E. The burst window has closed; retreat until your own cooldowns let you start a new exchange.
tips.heading: Remount reset

itemization.text: Start Doran's Blade with Shield Bash and Bone Plating. Bone Plating helps against his opening attacks, but you still need to avoid the fourth Violent Tendencies hit.
itemization.heading: Survive the entry

itemization.text: Choose Eclipse for shielded short trades or Voltaic Cyclosword for a sharper burst finish on dismounted Kled. Keep Flash and Teleport when you want a safer lane instead of gambling on an Ignite remount race.

keyTips.text: Sidestep the first Darkin Blade cast, dash past or around him to avoid the second sweet spot, and save a Q dash to kite away from the third cast.

keyTips.text: Track Umbral Dash ({cd:266:E}) above every other cooldown. When he spends it forward without landing the combo, that is your window to go in.

tips.text: If he misspaces a cast, answer with E into Q and a W trade, then leave sideways or backward depending on whether his dash is still up.

tips.text: Stay close enough to invade his space rather than eating blade tips at max range. Fighting on top of him shrinks the sweet spots you must dodge.

tips.text: Respect the post-6 all-in, and play tighter again at level 9 when his blade cooldown ({cd:266:Q}) drops sharply. Keep your own cooldowns up before trading into World Ender.

tips.text: Keep baiting blade casts without getting clipped. An Aatrox who whiffs casts and holds the third one too long has handed you the next trade.

tips.text: Win the dash economy: he repositions once per rotation while your Q, E and passive dashes keep resetting your angle. Longer trades favor the player still holding a dash.

tips.text: If a dash gets cancelled anyway, spend the next one escaping Infernal Chains sideways instead of re-engaging. Surviving his chain pull keeps the fight on your terms.

keyTips.text: Keep cooldowns to kite her ultimate. When Leap of Faith lands, leave the tentacle zone with dashes held for exactly this, and re-engage when it fades.

tips.text: Clear tentacles when safe. Walls near your turret grow her damage; kill lone tentacles between waves so her ultimate zone stays small.

tips.text: If her pull hits anyway, leave at once. Do not trade into the spirit; run out, break the tether, and accept the vessel pressure over a lost fight.

tips.text: After engaging with R, keep dashing around her. Test of Spirit can still be cast mid-fight, so circle her between combos instead of standing still to auto.

tips.text: Win fights she is not set up for. Without pre-placed tentacles her ultimate threatens little, and your R starts picks she cannot answer.

tips.text: Keep moving first. Crash waves and arrive at skirmishes before him; he wants grouped front-to-back fights where Call of the Forge God ({cd:516:R}) decides everything.

tips.heading: Team pivot

tips.heading: Pick clock

keyTips.text: Reserve a dash for Abduct, the chain cast after his initial E movement. Missing that second E is the opening you need to keep his trade from locking you into the rest of his damage.
keyTips.heading: Dodge the second E

keyTips.text: Use W for Kingslayer's damage after avoiding his chain. Do not spend your shield on a harmless approach and leave his point-blank W hit unanswered.
keyTips.heading: Shield Kingslayer

keyTips.text: When low-health Sylas is ready to Kingslayer, Ignite before he lands it. Applying healing reduction after the heal has already resolved wastes the timing that makes the finish reliable.
keyTips.heading: Ignite before the heal

tips.text: Identify whether Sylas is investing in W-E trades or Q waveclear. Your response changes with his ranks, and a favorable first exchange does not mean you can immediately repeat it while your cooldowns are longer.
tips.heading: Read the skill order

tips.text: Do not commit your important Q hit before checking whether he still has Abscond. His first E can dodge your damage even when you correctly save movement for his second E.
tips.heading: Account for his first dash

tips.text: After dodging Abduct, keep moving out of Chain Lash's delayed intersection explosion. Avoid winning the chain dodge only to stand still on the damage he left underneath you.
tips.heading: Leave the Q explosion

tips.text: As his W and E ranks and haste rise, separate your burst rotations with real disengages. Do not keep trading autos while your spells recover if his next Kingslayer and Abduct are already returning.
tips.heading: Repeated-cast pressure

tips.text: If he puts early ranks into Chain Lash to clear safely, play for wave pressure instead of pretending he has the same W-max threat. Reassess his trading strength from the spell he is actually leveling.
tips.heading: Q-max lane

tips.text: Keep your minion wave beside you when he jumps in. Make the short exchange happen with allied minion damage rather than following him into open lane for another free Kingslayer.
tips.heading: Fight with the wave

itemization.text: Use Doran's Shield for safer repeated trades or Doran's Blade when you can punish his misses. Eclipse supports shielded exchanges; Voltaic Cyclosword suits the burst route when you can finish before another Kingslayer.
itemization.heading: First-item choice

itemization.text: Executioner's Calling is useful even if you brought Ignite. Applying physical damage keeps healing reduction available for later Kingslayer casts rather than tying every winning trade to a summoner spell.
itemization.heading: Healing cut even with Ignite

keyTips.text: Never spend every cooldown while his E is ready. If he chases with spirit form up and yours are down, he runs you down; always hold an exit.

keyTips.heading: Cleave punish

tips.text: Take quick trades and get out. One short Electrocute combo, then leave before Lethal Tempo stacks turn his autos into the winning trade.
tips.heading: Quick trades

tips.text: Sidestep Mortal Steel thrusts. His stacked Q dash is his engage, so step sideways as the wind gathers and punish the missed dash.
tips.heading: Thrust sidestep

tips.text: Consider Exhaust for his all-ins. It blunts the Soul Unbound chase the same way it blunts other dash duelists, buying time for your cooldowns to return.
tips.heading: Exhaust option

tips.text: Even an item behind, he still wins your mistakes. One overstayed trade into his E lets him stat-check you, so keep the two-rotation rule: burst, leave, burst again.

tips.text: Respect his Death's Dance if he buys it. The bleed-out durability ruins one-shot math, so recalculate lethal before committing R to him.

tips.text: Win by kiting his spirit, then one-shotting late. Survive Soul Unbound, win two short rotations, and by late game delete him or his carries before Lethal Tempo matters.

keyTips.heading: No fist fights

keyTips.text: If Facebreaker grabs you, W immediately and E out of auto range. Lingering after the pull eats his full punch sequence for free.
keyTips.heading: Pull escape

keyTips.text: When he misses Facebreaker ({cd:875:E}), start a short trade and hold your W for his Haymaker answer. Your shield negates the return punch he relies on to flip losing trades.
keyTips.heading: Miss punish

tips.text: Treat the lane as reactive. Your wins come from his mistakes, so hold cooldowns and punish rather than forcing trades into his pull range.
tips.heading: Reactive lane

tips.text: He should never reach you without Facebreaker or Flash. If he is walking at you in auto range, your spacing already failed; reset range with a dash before trading.
tips.heading: Range reset

tips.text: Avoid the Facebreaker stun into Haymaker combo at all costs. Getting stunned inside his grit punch is the one sequence that loses an otherwise controlled lane.
tips.heading: Combo denial

tips.text: Play carefully after level 6. The Show Stopper ({cd:875:R}) gives him a second way to stick to you, so keep a dash reserved whenever his ultimate is up.
tips.heading: Post-6 care

tips.text: Answer his ultimate with your own: R behind yourself as he carries you, or time the blink to dodge the carry entirely, then kite out while his engage tools are spent.
tips.heading: Ult answer

tips.text: Outscale him through fights he cannot start. Without a landed pull he spectates while your R chooses the target, so group on your ultimate and deny him flanks onto you.
tips.heading: Fight scaling

tips.text: Respect him even when he is behind. A behind Sett still one-shots with a full-grit Haymaker and peels you off his carries with his ultimate, so never autopilot fights around him.
tips.heading: Behind respect

itemization.text: Eclipse first on the Conqueror line. Longer kited trades stack Conqueror while Eclipse shield covers the one pull combo you fail to space, unlike a pure burst build that dies to it.
Start Doran's Blade with Teleport and Flash. Blade supports Q-spacing trades from level 1, and Teleport insures against the single Facebreaker combo that would otherwise end your lane.

keyTips.text: Snowball before level 6. Kill her or build a big lead before Needlework arrives, because after 6 her ult slows and burst make your escapes cost dashes you need.
keyTips.heading: Pre-6 snowball

tips.text: Fight her early and often. Her early game is where your Electrocute combos out-trade her sustain, so press before her E all-in and stacks grow.
tips.heading: Early press

tips.text: Avoid extended trades at any point. Her passive percent-health autos win long fights, so land the shielded burst and dash out before she stacks on you.
tips.heading: No long trades

tips.text: Track her scissors stacks. A fully stacked Snip Snip is her trade threat; when stacks fall, step in and force the combo she cannot answer.
tips.heading: Stack watch

tips.text: Never let her split for free. She takes turrets and scales with gold faster than you, so match her wave, then move to fights while she is stuck clearing.

tips.text: Lethality punishes her better than bruiser when you dodge the mist. Burst her outside Hallowed Mist; if she mists well every time, bruiser durability keeps you alive longer.
tips.heading: Burst choice

tips.text: Win lane early, win fights late. Your lead must become R picks on her team before her scaling turns the side lane into a tax you cannot pay.
tips.heading: Lead conversion

tips.text: Kill her before the mist saves her. Full burst from outside Hallowed Mist, or hold damage until it fades; half combos inside the mist just feed her sustain.
tips.heading: Mist timing

keyTips.text: Dodge Path Maker above everything. His charged W is most of his damage and his stun; dash it sideways, but not so late that the cast cancels your dash.
keyTips.heading: Charge dodge

keyTips.text: Set up every Q with E first. Your E slow guarantees the sweet spot, and trading without it lets him walk out of your damage and answer freely.

keyTips.text: Escape All Out with your own ultimate. When he ults you through a wall, R straight back out instead of dueling his transformed damage.
keyTips.heading: Ult escape

tips.text: Accept losing priority to good K'Santes. His early trades are strong, so farm cleanly and take heavy trades only when Path Maker or his dash is spent.
tips.heading: Priority accept

tips.text: If he kidnaps you anyway, save abilities to escape. Getting carried toward his turret is survivable if your dashes are up; spending them first is not.
tips.heading: Kidnap escape

tips.text: Shield his Ntofo Strikes third hit. The knockup cast is his trade starter, so W as the empowered strike comes or dash before it lands.
tips.heading: Strike shield

tips.text: Scale to Black Cleaver and take over trades. Once Cleaver lands your combos shred his armor stacking and the lane flips in your favor.
tips.heading: Cleaver flip

tips.text: Beware his turret kidnaps forever. Even ahead, one Path Maker into All Out under his turret kills you, so crash waves from range and never linger at his wall.
tips.heading: Turret respect

tips.text: Win by making Path Maker whiff. Without his charged stun he cannot start the kidnap combo, and your Cleaver-scaled trades grind him out.
tips.heading: Whiff grind

tips.text: In fights, R carries past his peel. He wants to body-block and kidnap you; blink past him onto his backline and let your team handle the tank.
tips.heading: Past the tank

keyTips.text: At level 1, use Q reach to space outside his attacks. Aim to take no more than one Q-empowered attack rather than remaining close enough for both casts and ordinary autos.

keyTips.text: When Zaahen commits Grim Deliverance, aim R at his landing and disengage after your suppression ends. Use his committed landing to create an exit instead of staying for the renewed melee fight.

tips.text: Keep every trade short enough to leave before Zaahen sticks to you. Dreaded Return is the critical exit check, while later haste makes an old spacing advantage less reliable.

tips.text: Use W to absorb the Q hit you cannot space away from. The shield lets you answer a brief contact; it does not make standing beside him for the next Q cast safe.
tips.heading: Shield his Q

tips.text: When ahead, zone him away from minions before he can use The Darkin Glaive to recover health. Do not hand him free wave access between your short trades as the lane continues.

tips.text: After his first item, reassess Aureate Rush availability before trading forward. Haste can shorten the gap between his dashes; use {cd:904:E} as the base cooldown rather than assuming the first dash leaves a long escape window.

tips.text: End the exchange before your short trade becomes a full-Determination fight. His passive adds attack damage and enables a revive at full stacks, directly undermining a kill attempt based only on his visible health.

tips.text: Keep track of the second Darkin Glaive cast when choosing your exit. It knocks up, so do not wait beside him for the recast and expect a late dash to complete your retreat.
tips.heading: Second Q knockup
